articles.title: Smartphone prices surged around 17% in last 12 months, laptops and tablets rose 13.5% and 13.3%
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: With chipmaker SK hynix projecting memory demand to exceed supply through 2030, Techarc expects cost pressures on memory-intensive electronics to persist through 2027
A persistent global memory shortage has bifurcated India’s consumer technology market into two distinct price trajectories since November 2025, according to Techarc.

Tracking online prices for 1,097 products from January 2025 through October 2026, the study reveals that memory-heavy categories such as smartphones, laptops, tablets, smart TVs, routers, and security cameras, reversed course from declining trends to sharp price increases.
Smartphone prices, which dropped 7.3% between January and October 2025, surged 16.6% over the following 12 months. Laptops and tablets rose 13.5% and 13.3%, respectively.

Budget consumers face the sharpest impact because memory accounts for a higher percentage of total manufacturing costs in low-cost hardware. Entry-level smartphones (up to ₹12,000) jumped 21.9% on average, whereas premium models over ₹1 lakh fell 5.7%. The cheapest third of laptops and tablets rose 20.1% and 27.5%, respectively.
Market leaders like Samsung and Google kept smartphone price changes under 4%, while challenger brands raised prices by 14% to 22% as they relied more heavily on spot-market pricing.

Conversely, memory-light categories remained unaffected by this inflation which the research firm calls memflation (memory-led inflation). Wireless earbuds dropped 16.3%, robot vacuums fell 12.8%, and smartwatches declined 7.5%, driven by intense retail competition.
With chipmaker SK hynix projecting memory demand to exceed supply through 2030, Techarc expects cost pressures on memory-intensive electronics to persist through 2027.

articles.title: The changing scents of a warming world
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Be it in a forest or among the flowers in a garden, the air is enriched in volatile organic compounds, whose profiles climate change is beginning to alter

Being among herbs, shrubs, and trees is refreshing, both for the body and for the mind. In the 1980s, the Japanese popularised “shinrin-yoku” (forest bathing), which involved a quiet retreat into forests to soak in the air and listen to the life around you. Such retreats are even prescribed by doctors, as a form of preventive medicine. The practice is reminiscent of a stage of life called ‘Vanaprastha’ in ancient Hindu texts such as the Dharmasutras. More recently, the Forest Department of Uttarakhand has set up a forest healing centre near Ranikhet, where visitors are encouraged to leave their phones behind and absorb their natural surroundings.

Be it in a forest or among the flowers in a garden, the air is enriched in volatile organic compounds (VOCs). VOCs are carbon-containing molecules that evaporate easily at normal temperatures. Conifers such as cedars and pines are prodigious producers of VOCs, as are sal (‘shisham’ in Hindi; ‘chichamaram’ in Tamil) and the curry leaf tree (‘karivepillai’ in Tamil). In trees, VOCs are important compounds that ward off pests and pathogens. They also provide relief from environmental stress, especially heat and water stress during droughts. VOCs can also serve as signals, e.g. when plants release a molecular signature to warn nearby flora that they are being attacked by pathogenic fungi. Some of these compounds have antibacterial properties. Monoterpenes in conifers are an always-present barrier against attack. Wounded plants also begin secreting aldehydes that inhibit bacterial growth.

articles.title: All to play for: On the World chess championship in Geneva
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Chess is one sport where both the young and the old can excel

The World chess championship opened in Geneva with a game worthy of the occasion. Both the defending champion, D. Gukesh, and his challenger, Javokhir Sindarov, produced chess of top quality, and the draw was a just result . Given that the Indian was playing with black pieces and that he had gone into the match as the less favoured of the two, Gukesh could be a little happier with the game than his Uzbek rival. The Chennai Grandmaster was in considerable time trouble on multiple occasions, but managed to solve his problems and found proper answers to the questions posed to him on the board by the confident Sindarov. The match has only begun, and there is plenty of chess left. It is a long match of 14 games, played in the classical time control, and the man who reaches 7.5 points will be the champion. The well-contested opening game would have given Gukesh, and his team comprising his coach and ‘seconds’, enough confidence, after several disappointing performances since he became the youngest World champion in history , at 18, by defeating China’s Ding Liren in Singapore two years ago. That match too had gone down the wire, with Gukesh winning the last of the 14 games, thanks to a terrible mistake towards the end by his rival.

Sindarov is just six months older than Gukesh, making the Geneva match the youngest in the 140-year-old history of the World championship: both players are 20. It is remarkable that Gukesh has already seen the highs and lows of life at such a young age. For his opponent, the last one year has been better than a dream: from World No. 26 he has risen to No. 4. Chess is getting younger. The next World championship could also very well have two young contenders. Grandmasters are usually said to peak when they are around 30 and chess is one game that even older players have continued to excel in. Viswanathan Anand was 48 when he won the World rapid chess championship . The match between Gukesh and Sindarov has attracted considerable interest from across the sporting world. After the 1972 match between Boris Spassky and Bobby Fischer — the defining moment of world chess — the World championship has earned a reputation as one of the planet’s most important sporting events. No battle between two of the world’s most talented men in chess has ever disappointed.

articles.title: Transfer assumption: On the SAD(B)-BJP alliance in Punjab
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: BJP and SAD(B) cannot count on their support bases adding up

Few parties understand the arithmetic of the first-past-the-post (FPTP) system, and the necessity for alliances in States where they are minor players, better than the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) . The BJP has never shied away from partnerships with little ideological cohesion if they keep it electorally relevant. India’s FPTP system is unforgiving to smaller parties in a crowded polity if their support base is limited and dispersed. Votes translate into seats only if the support crosses a certain threshold. In Punjab , the BJP, despite its best efforts, has remained confined to sections of urban Hindu voters. Even after years of poaching leaders from the perennially fractious Congress , and after polling nearly a fifth of the vote in the 2024 general election without winning a seat, it realises that it cannot be relevant without a partner with a wider rural base. The Shiromani Akali Dal (Badal) walked out of the BJP -led National Democratic Alliance in 2020 over the Centre’s farm laws, which were later repealed, as the farmers’ agitation threatened its base in rural Punjab. But much water has flowed down the many rivers of the northern State since then. The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) has consolidated its hold in a crowded political space and is set to complete a full term. The Panthic vote, which used to be the SAD(B)’s core support base, has now fragmented. The SAD(B) appears to believe that it can regain ground only by expanding beyond its Panthic and rural constituencies, and that the farmers’ anger against the BJP is baggage from the past. It is this expedient calculation that now binds the two parties, despite six years of bitter attacks against each other. And it is also why the Union Home Minister, Amit Shah, has pointedly called the SAD(B) the “big brother” in Punjab after sealing the alliance.

The SAD(B)’s calculation may not work out as well as it hopes it would. Farmers’ anger against the BJP-led Centre has not entirely dissipated in rural Punjab. In earlier alliances, the two parties transferred votes to each other effectively, partly because their voters had fewer alternatives. But a revived Congress and an entrenched AAP have shown that they can win over urban Hindu voters wary of the Akalis and rural voters who are not inclined to back parties allied with the BJP. That these two sections will simply add up for the alliance is not certain. At best, the alliance consolidates enough of the anti-AAP vote to make this a clear three-cornered contest. Punjab is a sensitive border State and one of India’s granaries. It is also among India’s most indebted States, with a stagnating agrarian economy and a government that has expanded welfare expenditure despite strained finances. It needs a serious competition of ideas on what welfare it can afford and how to revive growth. The SAD(B)-BJP alliance , with its Panthic appeal on one side and Hindu consolidation on the other, instead offers a rehash of familiar identity politics. With AAP failing to deliver on governance, and the Congress stuck in its old ways, Punjab’s voters will have to decide who they dislike the least.

✍️ Editorial & Opinion 📅 29 Nov 2026 • IN-APP NEWSPAPER PRINT EDITION

Transfer assumption: On the SAD(B)-BJP alliance in Punjab

🎯 Exam Relevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary

BJP and SAD(B) cannot count on their support bases adding up

Few parties understand the arithmetic of the first-past-the-post (FPTP) system, and the necessity for alliances in States where they are minor players, better than the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) . The BJP has never shied away from partnerships with little ideological cohesion if they keep it electorally relevant. India’s FPTP system is unforgiving to smaller parties in a crowded polity if their support base is limited and dispersed. Votes translate into seats only if the support crosses a certain threshold. In Punjab , the BJP, despite its best efforts, has remained confined to sections of urban Hindu voters. Even after years of poaching leaders from the perennially fractious Congress , and after polling nearly a fifth of the vote in the 2024 general election without winning a seat, it realises that it cannot be relevant without a partner with a wider rural base. The Shiromani Akali Dal (Badal) walked out of the BJP -led National Democratic Alliance in 2020 over the Centre’s farm laws, which were later repealed, as the farmers’ agitation threatened its base in rural Punjab. But much water has flowed down the many rivers of the northern State since then. The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) has consolidated its hold in a crowded political space and is set to complete a full term. The Panthic vote, which used to be the SAD(B)’s core support base, has now fragmented. The SAD(B) appears to believe that it can regain ground only by expanding beyond its Panthic and rural constituencies, and that the farmers’ anger against the BJP is baggage from the past. It is this expedient calculation that now binds the two parties, despite six years of bitter attacks against each other. And it is also why the Union Home Minister, Amit Shah, has pointedly called the SAD(B) the “big brother” in Punjab after sealing the alliance.

The SAD(B)’s calculation may not work out as well as it hopes it would. Farmers’ anger against the BJP-led Centre has not entirely dissipated in rural Punjab. In earlier alliances, the two parties transferred votes to each other effectively, partly because their voters had fewer alternatives. But a revived Congress and an entrenched AAP have shown that they can win over urban Hindu voters wary of the Akalis and rural voters who are not inclined to back parties allied with the BJP. That these two sections will simply add up for the alliance is not certain. At best, the alliance consolidates enough of the anti-AAP vote to make this a clear three-cornered contest. Punjab is a sensitive border State and one of India’s granaries. It is also among India’s most indebted States, with a stagnating agrarian economy and a government that has expanded welfare expenditure despite strained finances. It needs a serious competition of ideas on what welfare it can afford and how to revive growth. The SAD(B)-BJP alliance , with its Panthic appeal on one side and Hindu consolidation on the other, instead offers a rehash of familiar identity politics. With AAP failing to deliver on governance, and the Congress stuck in its old ways, Punjab’s voters will have to decide who they dislike the least.

articles.title: DMK’s support for delimitation, stand on Thirupparankundram issue a ‘double betrayal’: VCK Minister Vanni Arasu
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Minister of Social Justice Department, Vanni Arasu, termed the DMK’s decision to support the Delimitation Amendment Bill and its position in the Thirupparankundram issue as “double betrayal”.
In a statement, Mr. Vanni Arasu said the VCK, which was part of the DMK alliance, had helped it defeat the Delimitation Amendment Bill in April 2026.

“The DMK played a significant role in voting against the Bill. A total of 352 members should have voted in favour for the Bill to secure a majority. However, only 298 members voted in its favour, resulting in the defeat of the 131st Constitutional Amendment Bill in Parliament. Even before this Bill was introduced, the then DMK government had moved a resolution in the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly on February 14, 2024. M.K. Stalin read out that resolution. It became the first resolution in India to expose the BJP’s conspiracy and all parties in the Assembly, including the VCK, supported and voted in favour of it, with the exception of the BJP,” he said.

He further said the DMK’s change of position “amounts to a betrayal” of Tamil Nadu. “The DMK has spoken about State rights throughout its existence. Now, it is willing to betray even the rights of the States,” he said.
He also flagged the DMK’s position in the Thirupparankundram case, alleging that it was maintaining a calculated silence.

“In the Thirupparankundram case, the Supreme Court’s verdict has been framed in a manner that threatens the rights of the State. The temple’s tradition is to light the sacred lamp at Thirupparankundram in accordance with Agama rules. Murugan devotees and the temple administration followed this practice in the past. The TVK government has now adopted the same position,” he said.

The Minister added, “Will the people of Tamil Nadu and secular forces forgive the DMK, a movement that once fought for State rights, for secretly joining hands with the BJP and becoming a ‘traitor’ to Tamil Nadu? History will never, ever forgive the DMK for this double betrayal – this double game.”

articles.title: Environmental conditions could contribute to breast cancer risk: Annamalai
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Survivors and volunteers of the organisation were present

Environmental conditions could contribute to breast cancer risk, said K. Annamalai, former IPS officer and founder of We the Leaders Foundation, at the 12th edition of ‘Engal Utsav’ in Chennai on Saturday.
The event was organised by Chennai Breast Centre and Sharana Breast Cancer Relief and Research Foundation, bringing together around 400 patients and survivors from across Tamil Nadu.

Two books, ‘The Healing Code: Lifestyle, Metabolism, Breast Cancer ’, by Selvi Radhakrishna, and ‘ Oru Sakthi Pirakkudhu Moochinile ’ , a collection of survivor stories by Sridevi Subramanian, were launched at the event. Mr. Annamalai, mentioning that his mother was also a breast cancer survivor, said that environmental conditions could contribute to the risk of breast cancer, apart from lifestyle factors. “Development cannot be measured by GDP alone. We also need more green spaces in our urban areas. Citizens must demand these essential deliverables from politicians and policymakers,” he said.

Dr. Selvi Radhakrishna said the annual gathering provided a space for patients at different stages of treatment and recovery to share experiences and draw strength from one another. “No one has to face the journey alone,” she said.

The expert sessions included ‘Beyond Cancer - Reclaiming You’ by plastic and reconstructive surgeon Venkat Ramakrishnan and ‘Busting Myths about Mammograms’ by radiologist Geethapriya. Other sessions featured naturopathy expert Roja Gurumurthy and carnatic vocalist Girija Rengarajan. Carnatic vocalist Gayathri Venkataraghavan presented a selection of compositions.
Survivors and volunteers of the organisation were present.

articles.title: Nainar Nagenthran accuses political forces of using Thirupparankundram for ‘minority votes’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: BJP Tamil Nadu president Nainar Nagenthran on Saturday accused political forces of attempting to portray Thirupparankundram Hill as ‘Sikandar Malai’ to secure minority votes and erase Hindu religious identities.

In a statement on November 28, he said the dispute over lighting the Karthigai Deepam at the deepathoon on Thirupparankundram Hill was about reclaiming the religious rights of lakhs of Murugan devotees.

He said that the Supreme Court’s interim order of November 20 had upheld the devotees’ long-standing demand to light the lamp at the deepathoon , which, he said, was located on land belonging to the Thirupparankundram temple.

Mr. Nagenthran accused the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam government of refusing to respect the court’s interim order and hurting the religious sentiments of devotees. He alleged that political forces had conspired to undermine Hindu religious identities in an attempt to secure minority votes.

“What will shine at the deepathoon on Thirupparankundram Hill today is not merely a lamp; it is the flame of victory for Murugan devotees. It is a reflection of the people’s faith in spirituality and the Constitution,” he said.

Responding to a question on VCK leader Thol. Thirumavalavan’s remarks that Thirupparankundram could become a zone of violence, Mr. Nagenthran, during a press interaction at Chennai airport on Saturday, said that if someone was predicting violence, it could mean that they were preparing to trigger it.
On Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s social media post saying ‘Arohara’, Mr. Nagenthran said the Prime Minister was entitled to chant ‘Arohara’ in praise of Lord Murugan as he was a Hindu.
He added that people belonging to any faith had the right to express their religious devotion, but no one should disparage another religion or disturb religious harmony.

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes

BJP Tamil Nadu president Nainar Nagenthran on Saturday accused political forces of attempting to portray Thirupparankundram Hill as ‘Sikandar Malai’ to secure minority votes and erase Hindu religious identities.

In a statement on November 28, he said the dispute over lighting the Karthigai Deepam at the deepathoon on Thirupparankundram Hill was about reclaiming the religious rights of lakhs of Murugan devotees.

He said that the Supreme Court’s interim order of November 20 had upheld the devotees’ long-standing demand to light the lamp at the deepathoon , which, he said, was located on land belonging to the Thirupparankundram temple.

Mr. Nagenthran accused the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam government of refusing to respect the court’s interim order and hurting the religious sentiments of devotees. He alleged that political forces had conspired to undermine Hindu religious identities in an attempt to secure minority votes.

“What will shine at the deepathoon on Thirupparankundram Hill today is not merely a lamp; it is the flame of victory for Murugan devotees. It is a reflection of the people’s faith in spirituality and the Constitution,” he said.

Responding to a question on VCK leader Thol. Thirumavalavan’s remarks that Thirupparankundram could become a zone of violence, Mr. Nagenthran, during a press interaction at Chennai airport on Saturday, said that if someone was predicting violence, it could mean that they were preparing to trigger it.

On Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s social media post saying ‘Arohara’, Mr. Nagenthran said the Prime Minister was entitled to chant ‘Arohara’ in praise of Lord Murugan as he was a Hindu.

He added that people belonging to any faith had the right to express their religious devotion, but no one should disparage another religion or disturb religious harmony.

articles.title: Bhupen Hazarika: The voice that gave philosophy a song
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: A hundred years after his birth, his songs remain alive not merely because of their unforgettable melodies or the extraordinary resonance of his voice, but because they continue to make us think about humanity, justice, identity, sacrifice and our responsibilities towards one another

There are artists whose greatness lies in the beauty they create and there are a rare few whose art enlarges our understanding of life itself. Bharat Ratna Dr Bhupen Hazarika belonged to the latter category. A hundred years after his birth, his songs remain alive not merely because of their unforgettable melodies or the extraordinary resonance of his voice, but because they continue to make us think about humanity, justice, identity, sacrifice and our responsibilities towards one another.

To describe Bhupen Da only as a singer would therefore be to diminish the vastness of his personality. He was a composer and lyricist, but also a poet, writer, journalist, filmmaker, scholar and public intellectual. Music, literature and cinema were not separate compartments of his creative life. They were different languages through which he pursued the same questions. What gives dignity to human life? Why does one human being remain indifferent to the suffering of another? What binds people divided by language, region or religion? What is the responsibility of the artist towards society?
Bhupen Da possessed the extraordinary gift of transforming such profound questions into songs that everyone could understand.

In Manuhe Manuhor Babe, and in its Bengali expression Manush Manusher Jonyo, an entire philosophy of human existence is distilled into one simple proposition: a human being must stand for another human being. There is no elaborate philosophical vocabulary, yet within those few words lies a powerful rejection of caste, creed, prejudice and indifference.

In Bistirno Paroreand later Ganga Behti Ho Kyun, a river becomes more than geography. It becomes a witness to civilisation. The river has seen suffering, inequality and injustice over generations and the poet questions its seemingly indifferent flow. Bhupen Da could take something as familiar as a river and make it the conscience of society. This was the profundity of his art: he could make philosophy sing.

articles.title: Changes in global garment sourcing trend to bring orders to Tiruppur
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Orders worth over ₹200 crore are said to have been shifted out of Bangladesh in November following labour unrest in that country, and a substantial part of it is expected to have come to India.
In Tiruppur, a major garment exporting cluster, exporters say it will take longer for the industries to benefit from diversion of orders from Bangladesh.

“Tiruppur should build its capacity to tap these opportunities,” said K.M. Subramanian, president of the Tiruppur Exporters Association (TEA). Large players are getting these orders now and are able to cater to the demands of the major brands, he added.

Raja Shanmugham, former president of the Association, said because of the disturbances in Bangladesh, and the good prospects of EU FTA coming into effect in the near future, several brands are starting to look for the right suppliers in India.
However, placement of orders will take place only in the coming months. The brands are exploring alternative sources now and the actual orders are likely to be finalised in March, he said.

Joint secretary of the TEA Kumar Duraiswamy explained that India’s trade agreements with the U.K. and the European Union in the last two years even as it negotiates a trade deal with the U.S. are throwing open opportunities for garment exporters. Global brands are looking at shifting their suppliers from China and Bangladesh for multiple reasons.

“Today, the dynamics of global sourcing are changing,” he said. Over the past year, these companies have been identifying new partners and upgrading existing production facilities to meet their specific requirements.

The U.S. continues to be a major destination for Indian exporters because the average annual spend of an American family in clothing and footwear ranges between $2,000 and $3,000, whereas it is just about $1,000 in the EU. Further, American buyers and brands are price conscious while the European brands look at compliances and audits.
While the U.S. will continue to be a major buyer of Indian garments despite the tariffs, several factories are also gearing up to meet the requirements of the EU buyers.
With the geopolitical developments affecting economies of many countries, European brands are also deferring taking delivery of the orders or cutting down on the orders across their supplier bases.

In the case of new suppliers, they are looking at a minimum 500 machines in a factory. Hence, while large companies are benefitting now from the orders diverted from Bangladesh, India SME factories should upgrade and work to tap these opportunities, he said.

articles.title: Experts say new U.S. tariffs do not pose substantial threat, India should not rush into trade deal
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: The latest proposal by the USTR takes the tariff framework on India back to what it was at the start of trade deal negotiations

The new 25% tariffs proposed by the U.S. on India do not pose a substantial risk to Indian exports, and India should go ahead with a trade deal only if it is balanced and reciprocal, according to exporters and trade and tariff experts.

An analysis of India’s trade relationship with the U.S. over the last two years showed that the latest tariffs announced by the U.S. have returned the tariff relationship to where it was at the start of trade deal negotiations.
The Office of the U.S. Trade Representative on Wednesday proposed a net tariff of 25% on goods imported from India, which could be reduced to 17% if a trade deal is signed by the two countries.

The proposed 25% tariff is nearly the same as the 26% tariff U.S. President Donald Trump had originally proposed in his ‘Liberation Day’ reciprocal tariff measure in April 2025. A week later, Mr. Trump paused these tariffs in a bid to secure trade deals with other countries.

In July 2025, he announced a 25% tariff on India, the same as what the USTR is now proposing. But Mr. Trump soon announced an additional 25% tariff as a penalty for India’s Russian oil imports taking the total tariff on Indian goods to 50%.

During that time, Mr. Trump also announced a 50% tariff on the import of steel and aluminium from all countries. The latest tariffs by the USTR are not in addition to those tariffs, meaning Indian steel and aluminium will continue to attract a 50% duty.

In February 2026, India and the U.S. issued a joint statement announcing the framework for an interim deal on trade, under which the U.S. would reduce its tariffs on Indian goods to 18%. This is very close to the 17% the U.S. is proposing now, should a deal be signed, nearly 10 months after the joint statement was issued.
As such, the pre-deal, post-deal, and steel and aluminium tariffs by the U.S. on India largely remain where they were at the start of negotiations.
Exporters and trade experts have said that India should proceed with a trade deal only if it satisfies Indian interests.

“FIEO supports the government’s efforts to conclude the Bilateral Trade Agreement at an early date,” said S.C. Ralhan, president of the Federation of Indian Export Organisations. “The agreement should be balanced and reciprocal, safeguard India’s long-term economic and developmental interests, and ensure that Indian exporters can compete on a level-playing field with suppliers from other countries in the U.S. market.”

The president of the PHD Chamber of Commerce and Industry, Anil Gupta, pointed out that the tariffs will have a limited impact on Indian exports due to the nature of the commodities that India predominantly exports to the U.S.

“India’s top exports to the U.S. include electronic goods, drugs and pharmaceuticals, gems and jewellery, and textiles and apparel,” Mr. Gupta said. “As these products account for more than 50% of Indian exports to the U.S. and are price-sticky, there will be limited impact in the short to medium term.”

articles.title: Broad-based pressure on food prices continues: RBI Bulletin
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: CPI inflation peaked to 6.1 % (y-o-y) in October 2026 from 5.5% in September 2026, slightly above the upper tolerance level of 6%–last observed in October 2024.
High-frequency data up to November 19 indicate continuing broad-based pressure on food prices, according to the November edition of the RBI Bulletin, released on Wednesday. .
Prices of all major cereals and pulses picked up. Edible oil prices recorded a broad-based increase, led by mustard oil, the RBI officials said in the State of the Economy article.

Vegetable prices presented a mixed picture, with onion prices rising moderately, tomato prices correcting sharply and potato prices picking up. The Indian basket of crude oil declined to $95 per barrel during November 1-18.
“The pressure on prices was primarily driven by ‘food and beverages’,” the officials pointed out.
Inflationary pressures were, however, not confined to food. Fuel and core inflation also firmed up, with 11 of the 12 CPI divisions registering sequential increases in October.

Within food and beverages, inflation rose across most sub-components, with notable spikes in vegetables, cereals, pulses and oils and fats, reflecting positive month-on-month price momentum. Fuel inflation recorded a relatively moderate uptick.

Geographically, inflation increased in both rural and urban areas in October, with food and beverages inflation remaining above 6% in both segments. While most States and Union Territories recorded inflation in the 4-6% range, the number reporting rates above 6% increased.

On the external front, geopolitical instability in West Asia continued to weigh on the global economic outlook. Although crude oil prices retreated from their October peaks, the absence of a durable peace kept markets volatile. “Apart from extant geopolitical risks, the recent pullback in AI stocks lends uncertainty to the global financial outlook,” the officials said.

Despite the challenging global environment and hawkish monetary policy stances adopted by major central banks, the RBI maintained that India’s domestic growth drivers and macroeconomic fundamentals remained important buffers.
“The Indian economy continues to maintain the resilience in economic activities as evident from high-frequency indicators,” they said.
“Strong bank and non-bank credit growth continues to support the domestic economy. Further, sustained double-digit export growth broadened the base of economic expansion,” they added.
Equity markets remained buoyant amid robust corporate earnings and foreign portfolio investment inflows, while net inflows through external commercial borrowings and NRI deposits remained strong.

Within food and beverages, inflation rose across most sub-components, with notable spikes in vegetables, cereals, pulses and oils and fats, reflecting positive month-on-month price momentum. Fuel inflation recorded a relatively moderate uptick.

Despite the challenging global environment and hawkish monetary policy stances adopted by major central banks, the RBI maintained that India’s domestic growth drivers and macroeconomic fundamentals remained important buffers.

“The Indian economy continues to maintain the resilience in economic activities as evident from high-frequency indicators,” they said.

“Strong bank and non-bank credit growth continues to support the domestic economy. Further, sustained double-digit export growth broadened the base of economic expansion,” they added.

Equity markets remained buoyant amid robust corporate earnings and foreign portfolio investment inflows, while net inflows through external commercial borrowings and NRI deposits remained strong.

articles.title: Net FDI fell to more than 5.5-year low in September 2026, as outflows jumped 40%
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: Despite September’s performance, net FDI in the first half of the financial year was more than 20% higher than in the same period last year

Net foreign direct investment (FDI) into India in September 2026 fell to its lowest level in at least 5.5 years, with outflows exceeding inflows by nearly $5 billion, data released by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) shows.

This was driven by a simultaneous slump in gross inflows and a jump in outflows. However, net FDI in the first half of the financial year (April-September 2026) was more than 20% higher than in the same period of the previous year.
September’s net FDI figure of -$4.95 billion was the lowest since at least March 2021, the earliest month for which data is accessible.

Direct investment refers to the inflows that give the investor substantial control over an asset or means of production, as opposed to portfolio investments, which are typically more in the nature of speculative purchases of minor shareholding.
Gross inflows, or the total amount of direct investment entering the country, fell to $5.9 billion in September 2026, 46.6% lower than in August, and 17.6% lower than in September of last year.

According to the RBI, around two-thirds of the gross inflows were channelled into manufacturing, communication, and computer services sectors, with Singapore and the U.S. as the major source countries.

Total outflows climbed to $10.8 billion in September 2026, nearly 40% higher than in August, and 15% higher than in September last year. Within this, repatriation of profits by foreign companies in India grew to $6.4 billion, nearly 37% higher than in the same month last year, and the highest since at least March 2021.
Outward investments made by Indian companies grew to a five-month high of $4.4 billion in September 2026.

The RBI says that of the outward investments, manufacturing, and financial, insurance and business services sectors accounted for about four-fifths of the amount that flowed out of India, with The Netherlands, Singapore and the U.S. serving as the major destinations.

articles.title: Duty-free raw sugar imports up to 10 lakh tonnes allowed till March 2027
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: The industry expects more imports in the coming days and this will ensure supply of adequate quantity of sugar in the domestic market throughout the sugar season.

Duty-free imports of up to 10 lakh tonnes of raw sugar will be permitted until the end of March 2027, according to a notification issued by the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) on Wednesday.

A notification issued on August 20 had allowed duty-free imports of up to 10 lakh tonnes of sugar under the Tariff Rate Quota (TRQ) scheme until December 31, 2026. Separately, the DGFT has allowed sugar mills time until September 30, 2027, to process the imported raw sugar and sell it in the domestic market.

The Indian Sugar and Bio-Energy Manufacturers Association Director General Deepak Ballani told The Hindu that price parity had prevailed over the past, making it viable for Indian importers to source raw sugar from international markets, primarily Brazil. Some imports have already begun.

The industry expects more imports in the coming days and this will ensure supply of adequate quantity of sugar in the domestic market throughout the sugar season. It will also keep the prices stable, he said.

articles.title: Magnitude 5 earthquake hits California: USGS
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The Los Angeles Fire Department, deploying personnel from 106 neighbourhood fire stations, determined no damage or injuries have been reported

An earthquake of preliminary magnitude 5 hit the area of Manhattan Beach, California, on Saturday morning (November 28, 2026), according to the United States Geological Survey. There were no immediate reports of injuries or damage.
The earthquake shook 5 kilometres southwest of Manhattan Beach, a city near Los Angeles, and caused multiple aftershocks in the area.

The Los Angeles Fire Department went into earthquake mode, deploying personnel from 106 neighbourhood fire stations to examine infrastructure for damage. The fire department determined no damage or injuries have been reported in the city of Los Angeles.

The City of Manhattan Beach urged residents to be prepared for aftershocks, which can occur minutes, hours and sometimes days after an earthquake. The city said on social media there is no tsunami threat at this time.

Teresa Macias had just gotten out of bed and made her coffee when her house in Lomita began to shake around 9:30 am local time. The painted bottles that she decorates fell to the floor, and her dog ran scared from underneath her bed.
As a Californian, Macias experiences earthquakes on a regular basis, but this one was different, the 66-year-old office clerk said.

“This one got everybody's attention. It was a big jolt, and the way it was moving the house, you knew that it was a 5-point something,” she said, adding that she continued to feel aftershocks over an hour after the initial earthquake.

articles.title: Fair play: on a hurried delimitation of Lok Sabha constituencies
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The government must build consensus on delimitation

The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) appears to have zeroed in on a hurried delimitation of Lok Sabha constituencies as the central piece of its strategy for the next general election, due in 2029. As the current constitutional scheme stands, a fresh delimitation is triggered once the data from the ongoing Census 2027 is published . That default path, which is based on population distribution across States, will considerably cut down the representation of States that have stabilised their population since the last delimitation. The Centre has now proposed to extend the constitutional freeze on inter-State distribution of Lok Sabha seats for another 25 years, until 2051, while increasing the size of the House to a maximum of 850 seats. The demarcation of the boundaries of Lok Sabha constituencies will be based on the 2011 Census within each State. The delimitation exercise will also bring into force 33% reservation for women , which Parliament approved in 2023. Considering the need to balance the ‘one person, one vote’ principle with the principles of federalism, which is about protecting the group rights of States, the proposals are a reasonable way forward for India. That said, the inter-State distribution of Lok Sabha seats is such a central question of democracy and federalism that any changes must be preceded by thoughtful deliberations at multiple levels.

That makes the approach of the Centre , which is trying to pass a constitutional amendment through defections and manipulations, dubious and lacking in good faith. If the Centre has been willing to extend the constitutional guarantee of inter-State distribution of seats on the basis of the 1971 Census, it could have built an all-party consensus on the issue . Instead, in April, it made a deceptive move by promising to maintain the current proportion of seats while the constitutional amendment it moved would have made that promise unconstitutional. At present, when the Centre is keen to appear accommodative, a more appropriate manner to proceed with such a generational measure in India’s federal democracy is to refer the Bills to a parliamentary committee that can examine them in detail and generate a national conversation. A bigger Lok Sabha will create its own challenges , while the case for increasing its size is not entirely without merit as India’s population has grown by at least 2.6 times since the 1971 Census, which forms the basis of the last delimitation of 1973, based on the 1971 Census. The Centre should not rush this vital question, which is not merely about garnering enough votes for passing a Bill. It must be based on consensus, as it happened in 1976 and again in 2001, under a Prime Minister from the Congress and one from the BJP, respectively.

articles.title: Transfer assumption: On the SAD(B)-BJP alliance in Punjab
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: BJP and SAD(B) cannot count on their support bases adding up

Few parties understand the arithmetic of the first-past-the-post (FPTP) system, and the necessity for alliances in States where they are minor players, better than the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) . The BJP has never shied away from partnerships with little ideological cohesion if they keep it electorally relevant. India’s FPTP system is unforgiving to smaller parties in a crowded polity if their support base is limited and dispersed. Votes translate into seats only if the support crosses a certain threshold. In Punjab , the BJP, despite its best efforts, has remained confined to sections of urban Hindu voters. Even after years of poaching leaders from the perennially fractious Congress , and after polling nearly a fifth of the vote in the 2024 general election without winning a seat, it realises that it cannot be relevant without a partner with a wider rural base. The Shiromani Akali Dal (Badal) walked out of the BJP -led National Democratic Alliance in 2020 over the Centre’s farm laws, which were later repealed, as the farmers’ agitation threatened its base in rural Punjab. But much water has flowed down the many rivers of the northern State since then. The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) has consolidated its hold in a crowded political space and is set to complete a full term. The Panthic vote, which used to be the SAD(B)’s core support base, has now fragmented. articles.title: Cultural values of language remain irreplaceable in AI era: Arabic meet
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Artificial Intelligence (AI) may transform the way Arabic is learned and used, but human emotions and traditional values remain beyond the reach of technology, an international conference on the Arabic language held at Anvarul Islam Arabic College, Kuniyil, observed on Thursday.

The two-day conference, titled ‘Digital humanities: reimagining Arabic language and literature’, was organised by the Arabic department of the college in association with Calicut University’s Arabic department, Kerala State Higher Education Council, and Arab Union of Internet Writers.
Liyaqat Ali, deputy director of collegiate education, inaugurated the conference on Wednesday. College Principal K. Mohammed Fawaz presided over the function.
Liyaqat Ali, deputy director of collegiate education, inaugurating an international conference on Arabic at Anvarul Islam Arabic College, Kuniyil, on Wednesday. | Photo Credit: SAKEER HUSSAIN

Arabic scholars Sumayya Ibrahim Abu Thailath from Palestine, Najeeb Ali Mulkhath from Yemen, Simi K. Salim, K. Ali Noufal, I.P. Abdul Salam, C.M. Sabir Navas, K.A. Nasser, P. Firoz, M.K. Ameer Swalahi, Shakir Babu Kuniyil, and K.P. Abdul Haleem Thangal spoke.
E.T. Mohammed Basheer, MP, inaugurated the valedictory function on Thursday. He highlighted the growing global significance of the Arabic language in an increasingly interconnected world.
Scholars Mujeeb Nellikkuth, Ali Jafar, Mohammed Aman K., P. Sulaiman and C. Abdul Wahab spoke.

articles.title: Kallakurichi TVK MLA Arul Vignesh arrested on charges of harassing IAS officer
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The TVK MLA was subsequently brought to the Circuit House in Kallakurichi on the Salem-Ulundurpet highway for questioning, where a large posse of police personnel has been deployed
A case was registered after the Madras High Court recently directed the State Public Prosecutor to get in touch with the officer regarding the allegations after she filed a formal police complaint .

Police sources said a team led by Shristi Singh, the Investigating Officer appointed by the Madras High Court , arrested the legislator at his residence in Kallakurichi on Friday evening and took him in a police vehicle. He was subsequently brought to the Circuit House in Kallakurichi on the Salem-Ulundurpet highway for questioning, where a large posse of police personnel has been deployed.

The Kallakurichi All Women Police, which had registered a sexual harassment case against the MLA, served summons on Mr. Vignesh on Wednesday directing him to appear for questioning in connection with the case. Speculation over his arrest grew after Inspector Bhuvaneshwari, attached to the All Women Police station, visited the MLA’s house in Kallakurichi on Wednesday (November 25) and handed the summons to him in person .

On 23.11.2026, a senior lady officer in Kallakurichi District preferred complaint against Thiru C. Arul Vignesh, MLA, Kallakurichi Constituency regarding alleged harassment and inappropriate conduct. On the same day, a case in Kallakurichi AWPS Cr No. 91/2026 was registered under appropriate sections of law. Initial investigation was done by the local police and on the directions of the Hon'ble High Court of Madras in WP (Crl) No. 3183/2026 dated 24.11.2026, Tmt. Shristi Singh, IPS, Superintendent of Police, Tiruppur District took investigation of this case under the supervision of Tmt. N. Kamini, IPS, Inspector General of Police, Administration, Chennai. During the investigation, the petitioner and other witnesses have been enquired by the Investigation Officer. Consequent to the enquiry, the alleged accused Thiru C. Arul Vignesh, MLA, Kallakurichi Constituency has been arrested and the investigation is under progress. Relating to this incident, 201 social media posts were pulled down by the local police and the Cyber Crime Department of Tamil Nadu Police. However, since the Hon'ble High Court has also ordered against publishing, communicating or making known to the public any of the matters covered under sections PoSH Act, it is requested to avoid posting any post in contravention to the above directions..
The police have booked a case against the MLA invoking provisions of the Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Harassment of Women Act and Sections 75, 78 and 79 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.

Tiruppur Superintendent of Police Ms. Singh began preliminary investigation into the incident on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) after receiving the inquiry report from Kallakurichi Superintendent of Police I. Shahnaz at the All Women Police Station.

Inspector General of Police (Administration) N. Kamini also visited Kallakurichi on Thursday (November 26) and supervised the investigation.

The opposition DMK, AIADMK, PMK and BJP had demanded his arrest after the incident came to light. The BJP Mahila Morcha also held Statewide protests on Friday (November 27), accusing the government of shielding the MLA.

The local police and the Cyber Crime Department had taken down 201 social media posts related to the incident, according to the police. The High Court has barred publishing, communicating or making public any matter covered under the PoSH Act, it said, urging the public not to post anything that violates these directions.

articles.title: Senior advocate Syed Faisal Qadri appointed as J&K’s Advocate General after two year gap
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Mr. Faisal is a designated senior advocate with over 20 years of practice; the Omar Abdullah government in April had proposed the names for the post while the appointment came after the J&K High Court heard a PIL plea on November 5 regarding the vacant post

Senior advocate Syed Faisal Qadri was on Friday (November 27, 2026) appointed as the Advocate General of Jammu and Kashmir, eight months after the J&K government forwarded the proposal to Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha for his approval. The J&K government has been without an Advocate General for more than two years.

“In exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (1) of Section 79 of the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019 (Act No. 34 of 2019) and in supersession of notification S.O. No. 07 of 2019 dated 01-11-2019, the Lieutenant Governor of the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir is pleased to appoint Mr. Syed Faisal Qadri, Senior Advocate, as Advocate General for the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir,” reads the official order.

Mr. Qadri is a designated senior advocate with over 20 years of practice. With over 100 reported judgments, Mr. Faisal earned a name for himself by pleading cases of both private and government institutions in the J&K High Court and in the Supreme Court.

The Omar Abdullah government in April this year had proposed the names for the post. The appointment, however, came after the J&K High Court heard a public interest litigation (PIL) petition on November 5 regarding the vacant post. Senior Additional Advocate General Monika Kohli had apprised the Division Bench, comprising Chief Justice Pushpendra Singh Bhati and Justice Rajnesh Oswal, that the appointment would be made within a period of one month.

It is a major relief for Chief Minister Omar Abdullah whose government was pursuing many pending policy matters before the J&K High Court in the past two years. Mr. Abdullah’s party National Conference (NC) had won the Assembly elections in 2024, but remained without an Advocate General since then.
In 2019, senior advocate D.C. Raina was appointed as the Advocate General of J&K. He, later, tendered his resignation in October 2024.

Mr. Faisal is a designated senior advocate with over 20 years of practice; the Omar Abdullah government in April had proposed the names for the post while the appointment came after the J&K High Court heard a PIL plea on November 5 regarding the vacant post

Senior advocate Syed Faisal Qadri was on Friday (November 27, 2026) appointed as the Advocate General of Jammu and Kashmir, eight months after the J&K government forwarded the proposal to Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha for his approval. The J&K government has been without an Advocate General for more than two years.

“In exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (1) of Section 79 of the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019 (Act No. 34 of 2019) and in supersession of notification S.O. No. 07 of 2019 dated 01-11-2019, the Lieutenant Governor of the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir is pleased to appoint Mr. Syed Faisal Qadri, Senior Advocate, as Advocate General for the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir,” reads the official order.

Mr. Qadri is a designated senior advocate with over 20 years of practice. With over 100 reported judgments, Mr. Faisal earned a name for himself by pleading cases of both private and government institutions in the J&K High Court and in the Supreme Court.

The Omar Abdullah government in April this year had proposed the names for the post. The appointment, however, came after the J&K High Court heard a public interest litigation (PIL) petition on November 5 regarding the vacant post. Senior Additional Advocate General Monika Kohli had apprised the Division Bench, comprising Chief Justice Pushpendra Singh Bhati and Justice Rajnesh Oswal, that the appointment would be made within a period of one month.

It is a major relief for Chief Minister Omar Abdullah whose government was pursuing many pending policy matters before the J&K High Court in the past two years. Mr. Abdullah’s party National Conference (NC) had won the Assembly elections in 2024, but remained without an Advocate General since then.

In 2019, senior advocate D.C. Raina was appointed as the Advocate General of J&K. He, later, tendered his resignation in October 2024.

articles.title: Centre proposes freeze on Lok Sabha seat proportions for States until 2051
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The new Constitutional Amendment Bill, accompanied by a fresh Delimitation Bill, proposes to increase the number of Lok Sabha seats in each State by 50%; they also bring into force the 33% reservation for women in the Lok Sabha

A new Constitutional Amendment Bill approved by the Union Cabinet on Friday (November 27, 2026) proposes an extension of the existing freeze on the inter-State distribution of Lok Sabha seats for another 25 years, until 2051, addressing the core concern of States that feared a loss of their proportionate strength due to the decline in their share of the national population.

The 132nd Constitutional Amendment Bill marks a significant turn from the 131st Amendment Bill moved by the Centre in April 2026 that sought to redistribute Lok Sabha seats among States according to the 2011 Census population.

The proposed amendment removes the linkage of the existing distribution of Lok Sabha seats to the 1971 Census and links it with provisions related to women’s reservation in Article 334A of the Constitution. The guarantee for a 50% increase in the number of Lok Sabha seats for each State is being written into this, providing that, for the purposes of giving immediate effect to such reservation for women, “the delimitation so undertaken shall provide for an increase of fifty per cent in the number of seats allocated to each State and Union territory in the House of the People.” The total number of seats in the Legislative Assembly of each State and Union territory will also increase similarly, “over and above the number of seats existing immediately before such delimitation”.

The new Bill, accompanied by a fresh Delimitation Bill, proposes to increase the number of Lok Sabha seats in each State by 50%, while the maximum strength of the lower House will rise from the current 550 to 850. If these Bills are passed by Parliament in its special sittings from November 30 to December 3, the path to immediate delimitation will open, which will also bring into force the 33% reservation for women in the Lok Sabha.
ALSO WATCH Cabinet clears delimitation Bill; is a two-thirds majority within reach? | Above the Fold | Nov 27, 2026

Amendments to Articles 81 and 82, which mandate the size and distribution of Lok Sabha seats among the States, propose to extend a sunset clause for the existing proportion until the first Census after 2051.

The existing provision in Article 82 that says that “until the relevant figures for the first census taken after the year 2026 have been published, it shall not be necessary to readjust” the distribution of seats is being amended in the Bill and will be changed to read “until the year 2051”.

Article 82 currently has two definitions for population: for the purposes of distribution among States, the 1971 population; and for the purposes of delimitation of individual constituencies within the States, the 2001 Census. The proposed amendment will extend the sunset clause to “until the year 2051”, but the reference to the 1971 Census has been dropped.

The Bill proposes that the distribution among States will be determined “in accordance with Article 334A”, while the boundaries of individual constituencies will be determined by the “latest published census figures available on the date of the commencement of the Constitution (One Hundred and Thirty-second Amendment) Act, 2026”.
ALSO WATCH Watch: Cabinet clears Delimitation Bill: 50% seat hike across states, special sitting Nov 30

articles.title: Lok Sabha seat freeze is no longer linked to population stabilisation
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The distribution of seats based on 1971 Census continued for 50 years for the reason that a readjustment would adversely affect the proportion of States that stabilised population. Population stability was a stated objective of the government. That link between population stability and Lok Sabha share has been removed in the 132nd Constitutional Amendment Bill

The amendments in the Constitution being proposed in a Bill approved by the Union Cabinet propose to continue the existing proportion of strength in the Lok Sabha of individual States for another 25 years, until 2051.

The existing distribution of Lok Sabha seats was based on the population distribution recorded in the 1971 Census, and determined in the delimitation of 1973. That distribution continued for 50 years for the reason that a readjustment would adversely affect the proportion of States that stabilised population. Population stability was a stated objective of the Indian government. That link between population stability and Lok Sabha share has been removed in the proposed 132nd Constitutional Amendment Bill. The freeze on proportion will continue for another 25 years, as a special measure to accommodate 33 per cent seats for women.

articles.title: Navy Project 17A programme completed as GRSE hands over final stealth frigate Vindhyagir
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Vindhyagiri (Yard 3024) is the third and final Project 17A frigate built by GRSE

The Indian Navy on Friday (November 27, 2026) received Vindhyagiri, the seventh and final ship of the Nilgiri-class (Project 17A) stealth frigates, from Garden Reach Shipbuilders and Engineers Ltd (GRSE) in Kolkata, marking the completion of the Project 17A ship delivery programme and a significant milestone in India’s indigenous warship construction capabilities.

Vindhyagiri (Yard 3024) is the third and final Project 17A frigate built by GRSE. With its delivery on Friday (November 27, 2026), all seven ships under the programme have been handed over to the Navy within 23 months of the delivery of the first ship, INS Nilgiri, on December 20, 2024, the Defence Ministry said.

Designed by the Navy’s Warship Design Bureau and overseen by the Warship Overseeing Team in Kolkata, the Project 17A frigates represent a generational leap in indigenous warship design, stealth, survivability and combat capabilities.

The multi-mission platforms are equipped with an advanced suite of weapons and sensors, enhancing their capabilities across anti-surface, anti-air and anti-submarine warfare domains. They also feature Combined Diesel or Gas (CODOG) propulsion systems, comprising a diesel engine and a gas turbine, along with an Integrated Platform Management System.

The construction period of Vindhyagiri was reduced to 68 months, compared with 84 months taken for the first-of-class INS Nilgiri, reflecting the experience gained during the construction of the preceding six ships.

Named after the Vindhyagiri mountain range in Karnataka, the frigate is a reincarnation of the erstwhile INS Vindhyagiri, a Leander-class frigate that served the Navy for 31 years, from July 8, 1981, to June 11, 2012.

With an indigenous content of 75%, the Project 17A programme involved more than 200 micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs). It generated employment for approximately 4,000 personnel directly and over 10,000 indirectly.
The delivery underscores the Navy’s focus on Aatmanirbharta in warship design and construction, while highlighting the country’s growing capabilities in complex naval shipbuilding.

articles.title: Broad-based pressure on food prices continues: RBI Bulletin
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: CPI inflation peaked to 6.1 % (y-o-y) in October 2026 from 5.5% in September 2026, slightly above the upper tolerance level of 6%–last observed in October 2024.
High-frequency data up to November 19 indicate continuing broad-based pressure on food prices, according to the November edition of the RBI Bulletin, released on Wednesday. .
Prices of all major cereals and pulses picked up. Edible oil prices recorded a broad-based increase, led by mustard oil, the RBI officials said in the State of the Economy article.

Vegetable prices presented a mixed picture, with onion prices rising moderately, tomato prices correcting sharply and potato prices picking up. The Indian basket of crude oil declined to $95 per barrel during November 1-18.
“The pressure on prices was primarily driven by ‘food and beverages’,” the officials pointed out.
Inflationary pressures were, however, not confined to food. Fuel and core inflation also firmed up, with 11 of the 12 CPI divisions registering sequential increases in October.

Within food and beverages, inflation rose across most sub-components, with notable spikes in vegetables, cereals, pulses and oils and fats, reflecting positive month-on-month price momentum. Fuel inflation recorded a relatively moderate uptick.

Geographically, inflation increased in both rural and urban areas in October, with food and beverages inflation remaining above 6% in both segments. While most States and Union Territories recorded inflation in the 4-6% range, the number reporting rates above 6% increased.

On the external front, geopolitical instability in West Asia continued to weigh on the global economic outlook. Although crude oil prices retreated from their October peaks, the absence of a durable peace kept markets volatile. “Apart from extant geopolitical risks, the recent pullback in AI stocks lends uncertainty to the global financial outlook,” the officials said.

Despite the challenging global environment and hawkish monetary policy stances adopted by major central banks, the RBI maintained that India’s domestic growth drivers and macroeconomic fundamentals remained important buffers.
“The Indian economy continues to maintain the resilience in economic activities as evident from high-frequency indicators,” they said.
“Strong bank and non-bank credit growth continues to support the domestic economy. Further, sustained double-digit export growth broadened the base of economic expansion,” they added.
Equity markets remained buoyant amid robust corporate earnings and foreign portfolio investment inflows, while net inflows through external commercial borrowings and NRI deposits remained strong.

articles.title: Net FDI fell to more than 5.5-year low in September 2026, as outflows jumped 40%
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: Despite September’s performance, net FDI in the first half of the financial year was more than 20% higher than in the same period last year

Net foreign direct investment (FDI) into India in September 2026 fell to its lowest level in at least 5.5 years, with outflows exceeding inflows by nearly $5 billion, data released by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) shows.

This was driven by a simultaneous slump in gross inflows and a jump in outflows. However, net FDI in the first half of the financial year (April-September 2026) was more than 20% higher than in the same period of the previous year.
September’s net FDI figure of -$4.95 billion was the lowest since at least March 2021, the earliest month for which data is accessible.

Direct investment refers to the inflows that give the investor substantial control over an asset or means of production, as opposed to portfolio investments, which are typically more in the nature of speculative purchases of minor shareholding.
Gross inflows, or the total amount of direct investment entering the country, fell to $5.9 billion in September 2026, 46.6% lower than in August, and 17.6% lower than in September of last year.

According to the RBI, around two-thirds of the gross inflows were channelled into manufacturing, communication, and computer services sectors, with Singapore and the U.S. as the major source countries.

Total outflows climbed to $10.8 billion in September 2026, nearly 40% higher than in August, and 15% higher than in September last year. Within this, repatriation of profits by foreign companies in India grew to $6.4 billion, nearly 37% higher than in the same month last year, and the highest since at least March 2021.
Outward investments made by Indian companies grew to a five-month high of $4.4 billion in September 2026.

The RBI says that of the outward investments, manufacturing, and financial, insurance and business services sectors accounted for about four-fifths of the amount that flowed out of India, with The Netherlands, Singapore and the U.S. serving as the major destinations.

articles.title: Duty-free raw sugar imports up to 10 lakh tonnes allowed till March 2027
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: The industry expects more imports in the coming days and this will ensure supply of adequate quantity of sugar in the domestic market throughout the sugar season.

Duty-free imports of up to 10 lakh tonnes of raw sugar will be permitted until the end of March 2027, according to a notification issued by the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) on Wednesday.

A notification issued on August 20 had allowed duty-free imports of up to 10 lakh tonnes of sugar under the Tariff Rate Quota (TRQ) scheme until December 31, 2026. Separately, the DGFT has allowed sugar mills time until September 30, 2027, to process the imported raw sugar and sell it in the domestic market.

The Indian Sugar and Bio-Energy Manufacturers Association Director General Deepak Ballani told The Hindu that price parity had prevailed over the past, making it viable for Indian importers to source raw sugar from international markets, primarily Brazil. Some imports have already begun.

The industry expects more imports in the coming days and this will ensure supply of adequate quantity of sugar in the domestic market throughout the sugar season. It will also keep the prices stable, he said.

articles.title: U.S. disables ship trying to leave Iran, as Tehran vows to confront blockade
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Mohammad Mokhber, an adviser to ⁠Iran’s Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, said: “Neither will the Strait of Hormuz be ‌reopened, nor will we allow the blockade to remain in place,” Iranian state media reported

The U.S. military said on Friday (November 27, 2026) ‌it disabled a commercial ship on Thursday (November 26, 2026) ​after it attempted to ⁠run the US blockade of Iran, while an adviser to the Iranian supreme leader ‌said Iran would keep the Strait of Hormuz shut ‌while vowing to break the embargo.

CENTCOM disabled a commercial vessel in the Gulf of Oman, Nov. 26, after the crew attempted to run the U.S. naval blockade, despite multiple warnings, following departure from Bandar Abbas. A U.S. military aircraft launched precision munitions that struck the stern of Palau-flagged M/V Pacific Archer. The ship's propulsion was ultimately disabled and the civilian crew was unharmed. Read the full release online: https://t.co/4CAaN4gDvW

The ‌U.S. ⁠Central Command said in ⁠a statement that military aircraft launched precision munitions that struck the stern of the Palau-flagged M/V ​Pacific Archer ‌in the Gulf of Oman after it departed from the Iranian port city of Bandar Abbas, and ‌the ship’s propulsion was disabled while ​the civilian crew was unharmed.

Meanwhile, Mohammad Mokhber, an adviser to ⁠Iran’s Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, said: “Neither will the Strait of Hormuz be ‌reopened, nor will we allow the blockade to remain in place,” Iranian state media reported. He did not give details of Iran’s plans for breaking the embargo.

The U.S. ‌reimposed its naval blockade on Iranian ports ​in July, and earlier this month announced Task Force Iron ⁠Gate to restrict the movement of weapons ⁠and sanctioned materials across Iran’s land borders and the Caspian ‌Sea.

articles.title: Global fashion brands shift orders from Bangladesh to India amid unrest
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Between November 1 and 18, brands diverted about $254 million worth ⁠of orders from Bangladesh, with most moving to neighbouring India, the owners said

Global fashion retailers including Zara and H&M shifted nearly a tenth of their monthly orders from ‌Bangladesh to other Asian manufacturing hubs in the first half of November, as labour unrest disrupted production and rising ​costs eroded the country’s competitive edge, three factory owners said.

Between November 1 and 18, brands diverted about $254 million worth ⁠of orders from Bangladesh, with most moving to neighbouring India, the owners said, a shift that represents a major blow to a key pillar of Bangladesh’s economy and could extend beyond the current unrest.

Industry leaders have said rising wages, energy shortages and political uncertainty have weakened the low-cost advantage that helped ‌make Bangladesh the world’s second apparel exporter after China, prompting global brands to diversify sourcing.

The protests have caused more than $400 million in production losses, according to the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA), in an industry that accounts for more ‌than 80% of Bangladesh’s export earnings and nearly 40% of its manufacturing jobs.
India has emerged ‌as ⁠the biggest beneficiary, while buyers are also looking to Vietnam, Cambodia and Indonesia to reduce supply-chain risks and improve delivery ⁠reliability, industry leaders said.
Those pressures intensified on Wednesday when Bangladesh approved a 36% increase in the minimum wage for garment workers, the smallest rise in four decades.

The increase fell well short of workers’ demands to more than double wages, triggering fresh clashes with police even as Abdur Rahman Tarafder, secretary of the Ministry of Labour and Employment, ​said the wage increase was “satisfactory” and that he hoped all ‌workers would resume work from Saturday.
Industry leaders said the increase would nevertheless narrow Bangladesh’s labour-cost advantage over India, although union groups argue the wages remain low by global industry standards.
Babul Akhter, a union leader and workers’ representative on the government-appointed wage board, said brands should not use the unrest to justify shifting orders out of Bangladesh.

He said retailers already factor political instability and labour ‌unrest into sourcing decisions, making such moves “hard to justify” and raising “serious doubts” whether the unrest was more than an excuse.

Factory ​owners, speaking on condition of anonymity because of concerns about their relationships with international buyers, said the unrest had prompted Zara, H&M, Marks & Spencer, Celio and other global brands to divert orders, with India receiving the bulk of ⁠the business.
Zara owner Inditex declined to comment on Reuters’ questions, while M&S, H&M and Celio did not respond to requests for comment.

articles.title: Accused shot during exchange of fire with police West Bengal’s Asansol
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The dramatic operation unfolded in the congested neighbourhood, with armed police personnel in plain clothes searching narrow lanes and houses, and climbing boundary walls to trace the accused

An accused wanted in multiple cases in West Bengal’s Asansol, was on Friday (November 27, 2026) shot in his right leg during an alleged clash leading to an exchange of fire with the police when they went to arrest him on Friday morning. The accused, Pratap Das, is wanted in several cases of robbery, theft, iron smuggling, and cyber fraud across Asansol. Police have been searching for him for the past few days in connection with a cyber fraud case lodged last week at Asansol South Police Station. When the police went to arrest him on Friday (November 27, 2026) from a hideout in the Ismail area, he opened fire at the police team. Later, he was shot in retaliatory fire.
According to the police, an operation to arrest Pratap was launched on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) when he again opened fire at the police team upon spotting them and managed to flee.

The operation was launched by the Asansol Durgapur Police Commissionerate Special Operations Group (SOG), along with officers from Hirapur police station, following a tip-off that he was hiding in the area and carrying a firearm. The dramatic operation unfolded in the congested neighbourhood, with armed police personnel in plain clothes searching narrow lanes and houses, and climbing boundary walls to trace the accused.

Shots of firing were heard in broad daylight causing panic among residents who witnessed a cat and mouse chase between the accused and police. The accused was seen being dragged from one of the houses out by the police with blood dripping from his right leg and was carried on all fours to a police vehicle.

Local residents in the area said that they had no idea about the accused. “We did not know that he was hiding in our neighbourhood. I went to drop my daughter off at school when I saw police chasing him. It was scary,” said a woman who stays in the area from where Pratap was arrested.

Association for Protection of Democratic Reforms, a civil rights group raised questions about the manner in which police paraded in groups with weapons. “Instead of relying on intelligence inputs, a scientific approach, and proper procedures to apprehend the criminal, the police’s actual objective was to intimidate the general public through a display of firepower,” APDR vice president Ranajit Sur said.

The development comes after a total of five encounters that took place in West Bengal since the new Bharatiya Janata Party government came to power. Five people who have been shot dead by the police during these incidents include three accused in rape cases of minors and two accused of murder.

The dramatic operation unfolded in the congested neighbourhood, with armed police personnel in plain clothes searching narrow lanes and houses, and climbing boundary walls to trace the accused

An accused wanted in multiple cases in West Bengal’s Asansol, was on Friday (November 27, 2026) shot in his right leg during an alleged clash leading to an exchange of fire with the police when they went to arrest him on Friday morning. The accused, Pratap Das, is wanted in several cases of robbery, theft, iron smuggling, and cyber fraud across Asansol. Police have been searching for him for the past few days in connection with a cyber fraud case lodged last week at Asansol South Police Station.
