articles.title: AIDSO students stage protests in Shahabad and Hosapete in support of ASHAs agitation
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Students belonging to the All India Democratic Students’ Organisation (AIDSO) staged protests in Shahabad in Kalaburagi district and Hosapete in Vijayanagara district on Saturday, expressing solidarity with Accredited Social Health Activists (ASHAs) who have been staging an indefinite protest in Bengaluru for the past 12 days, demanding a monthly honorarium of ₹15,000.

In Shahabad, students staged a demonstration at Nehru Circle, while in Hosapete, the protest was held in front of the taluk office. The students urged the State government to fulfil the demands of the ASHAs, who are protesting under the leadership of the All India United Trade Union Centre (AIUTUC) at Freedom Park in Bengaluru.

Addressing the protesters in Shahabad, AIDSO district secretary Venkatesh Devadurga said thousands of ASHA workers were continuing their agitation despite the rain and cold, with some bringing their young children to the protest venue. He said their struggle for fair remuneration and recognition of their services was an inspiration to all those fighting for justice.

He recalled that the State government had promised to provide a monthly honorarium of ₹10,000 following an earlier protest by ASHAs two years ago. “However, the promise had not been fulfilled. The activists were right in insisting on a government order rather than accepting fresh assurances,” he said.
He urged the Chief Minister and the Health Minister to stop making what he termed insensitive remarks and resolve the issue by accepting the workers’ demands.

AIDSO district vice-president Govind Yalawar, speaking at the Shahabad protest, condemned the government for failing to address the concerns of ASHAs, who walk long distances every day to provide healthcare services to people. “While the government has resources to extend financial concessions to large corporate houses, it is reluctant to provide adequate remuneration to ASHAs,” he said.

In Hosapete, AIDSO Vijayanagara district president Ravikiran J.P. said nearly 42,000 ASHAs across Karnataka had been participating in the agitation for the past 12 days. “ASHAs are currently receiving only ₹5,000 a month from the State government. They are demanding a written government order, as an earlier assurance to provide an honorarium of ₹10,000 a month had not been implemented even after two years,” he said.

He also criticised the government’s response to the agitation, stating that ASHAs had played a significant role in delivering healthcare services, reducing maternal and infant mortality and providing services during the COVID-19 pandemic. “Their contribution had been widely acknowledged, but their demand for a minimum monthly honorarium of ₹15,000 was yet to be accepted,” he said.

AIDSO district secretary U. Umadevi, speaking at the Hosapete protest, said the organisation was drawing inspiration from the struggle of ASHAs and would continue to oppose policies that threatened the public education system.
The Hosapete protest was also held to mark the death anniversary of social reformer Mahatma Jyotirao Phule.

articles.title: Pawan Kalyan expresses grief over livestock deaths in Kakinada district
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: He directs Collector to inquire into the fire accident and ensure compensation to the affected farmer.

Andhra Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister Pawan Kalyan has expressed grief over the death of livestock and poultry in a fire accident at Narasingapuram village in Pithapuram mandal of Kakinada district in the early hours of Saturday.

The fire broke out in a thatched shed belonging to dairy farmer Kottem Dharmarao, killing seven buffaloes, six calves and around 30 chickens. The District Collector briefed the Deputy Chief Minister on the incident.
Preliminary information suggests that the fire may have originated in the thatched structure. Fire services personnel are investigating the cause of the accident.

Expressing concern over the farmer’s loss of livelihood, Mr. Pawan Kalyan directed the Collector to conduct an immediate inquiry and submit a report. He also instructed officials to take necessary steps to extend government assistance and ensure that the affected farmer receives compensation.

articles.title: Thirupparankundram row LIVE: Karthigai lamp lit at 'deepathoon'; Supreme Court appointed retired Judges oversee the ceremony
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Supreme Court declared that Executive authorities had wilfully disobeyed the orders of the court over the failure to light the ceremonial Karthigai Deepam at the disputed stone pillar on Thirupparankundram
Devotees were seen to be celebrating the lighting of the Karthigai lamp at the ‘deepathoon’ an hour after the event ended.
Hindu outfits including the BJP raised ‘Arohara’ slogans for Madras Hight Court Judge G.R. Swaminathan, the Supreme Court and CRPF personnel.

Somaskandan, a priest, who lit the lamp at ‘deepathoon’, said it was a very exciting experience to do so as per the Supreme Court order. All rules of the court were followed and it showed the will of the devotees, he added.

‘We The Leaders’ founder K. Annamalai, speaking to reporters at the Coimbatore airport, said the Supreme Court’s directive permitting the lighting of the ceremonial lamp at the stone pillar was “not a verdict to be celebrated,” as it merely affirmed the right of worship for devotees of Lord Murugan.

Noting that Muslims visit the dargah on the hill while Hindu devotees light the lamp at the stone pillar, he said the matter should end there and warned that repeatedly dragging it out would only lead to unnecessary untoward consequences.

Mr. Annamalai described the conduct of the event under Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) security as a bad precedent that should not have occurred, blaming the State Government and urging it to introspect.
Following the Karthigai lamp lighting at ‘deepathoon’, devotees were seen to be thanking the CRPF personnel outside the Thirupparankundram temple.
Amid tight security by armed CRPF personnel and chants of ‘Vetrivel, Veeravel,’ (Victory to Lord Muruga’s spear, Hail the valourous spear of the lord), the lamp was lit.
Enthusiastic devotees also chanted ‘Vetrivel Muruganukku Arohara’ (Salutations to Lord Muruga, who holds the victorious spear).
A large gathering of devotees witnessed the spectacle of lamp lighting atop the ‘deepathoon’ at Thirupparankundram foothills and many of them were seen turning emotional after the lamp was lit.

One of the Supreme Court appointed Receivers and retired Judge of Madras High Court, V. Parthiban said, “It was an out-of-the-world experience”, on witnessing the lighting of Karthigai lamp on ‘deepathoon’ atop the Thirupparankundram hillock.
BJP state secretary Vinoj P. Selvam lit a lamp resembling ‘deepathoon’ at Purasaiwakkam.

articles.title: Delimitation Bill unscientific, will hurt southern States, says Priyank Kharge
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The proposed delimitation Bill of the Narendra Modi-led Union government is unscientific and politically motivated and could undermine the political representation of southern States, Home Minister Priyank Kharge has alleged.

Addressing a media conference at Aiean-e-Shahi Guest House here on Saturday, Mr. Kharge said Mr. Modi was pushing the proposal out of fear of electoral defeat and was seeking to retain power by altering the electoral landscape to suit his political interests.

He questioned the rationale behind increasing the number of Lok Sabha seats from the present 543 to around 850. If delimitation was carried out primarily on the basis of population, southern States that had made significant progress in population control, education, healthcare and economic development could be penalised with reduced political representation, he said.

“Even with 543 members, Parliament is unable to address people’s problems adequately. What difference would increasing the number of seats to 800 or 900 make?” he asked, demanding that the Union government explain the benefits of the proposed increase.

He stressed that the delimitation process should be free from government influence and take into account geographical conditions, administrative convenience and social justice. He also sought clarity on the composition and powers of the Delimitation Commission, including the voting rights of its members.

Questioning the proposal to give the Chief Election Commissioner voting rights in the commission, he asked whether it was appropriate to assign such a decisive role to the head of the Election Commission, particularly when the process of appointing the Chief Election Commissioner itself had been changed.

He also questioned the Centre’s urgency in undertaking delimitation on the basis of the 2011 Census and sought clarity on the criteria to be followed for reservation and representation of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Other Backward Classes and women.
He called upon southern States to unite against any move that could affect their interests and said political parties should set aside differences when the interests of the State were at stake.
On the drinking water situation in the State, Mr. Kharge said the government was extending assistance even in areas where gram panchayats were not functioning effectively.

“However, there were limits to what the government could do when natural conditions affected the availability of water. Even in places such as Mangaluru and Udupi, water could not always be secured despite the availability of funds. A task force had been constituted to address drinking water problems, and the government was ready to provide additional funds wherever necessary. Legislators had also been given the freedom to take measures suited to the conditions in their constituencies,” he said.
Mr. Kharge said a request had been made to the Chief Minister for the release of water into the Bhima river, while the Chief Secretary had also held discussions with officials in Maharashtra.
“The State government was in constant touch with the Maharashtra government and will pursue a united legal battle to protect Karnataka’s interests,” he said.

articles.title: Delimitation in India’s strategic periphery: a national security blind spot
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The old Jammu-Poonch constituency was never the preserve of a single political formation

The debate over delimitation in India is generally framed around equal representation and changing population patterns. Yet, in strategically sensitive regions, redrawing electoral boundaries has implications that extend well beyond electoral arithmetic. As Parliament considers a fresh delimitation initiative, Jammu and Kashmir offers an important case study of how constituency restructuring can reshape political geography, regional relationships and, ultimately, the strategic considerations underpinning national security.

While the delimitation of individual Assembly constituencies in Jammu and Kashmir and Assam attracted considerable public and political attention in 2022–23, far less scrutiny was devoted to the restructuring of the Anantnag and Jammu-Poonch Lok Sabha constituencies. articles.title: Israeli strike kills two Doctors Without Borders staff in Gaza
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: MSF said the two men, who worked as security guards at a clinic, were killed in “a direct hit”, while the Israeli army called them Hamas “terrorists”
Doctors Without Borders (MSF) said on Saturday (November 28, 2026) an Israeli strike killed two staff members at a clinic in Gaza, with the Israeli army labelling the pair as Hamas “terrorists”.

The Israel Defence Forces (IDF) identified the men, who worked as security guards at the clinic, as Hamas artillery cell commander Moaz Yousef Alitsbach and Ahmed Sufyan Muhammad Ali Abu. MSF said it was “devastated” by the killings, and denounced “a direct hit” on the organisation.
“Our premises were clearly marked with MSF logos, and their location had been communicated to and was known by the Israeli military,” it wrote on X.

World Health Organization chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus condemned the attack. “Attacks on health facilities, health workers and humanitarian personnel in #Gaza are outrageous and unacceptable,” he posted on X.

The IDF denied targeting a hospital or damaging medical infrastructure. “This is another example of the Hamas terrorist organization embedding itself within international organizations,” it posted on Telegram.

articles.title: Autoimmune conditions can be managed well with early diagnosis and treatment: experts
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: At The Hindu’s webinar, they stressed the importance of not ignoring symptoms that lasted for more than a few weeks

When autoimmune conditions are diagnosed early and appropriate treatment is started, they can be well managed and patients can lead full, productive lives, said doctors, speaking at The Hindu ’s webinar on ‘Understanding Autoimmune Conditions’ held on Saturday (November 28, 2026). Autoimmune conditions occur when the immune system mistakenly attacks the body’s own tissues and organs.

Aishwarya G., consultant rheumatologist and clinical immunologist, Apollo Specialty Hospitals, Chennai, explained the hows and whys. She said genes, the environment, hormones, and lifestyle all played a part, and discussed early warning symptoms. She stressed that these conditions were not contagious and that nothing that patients did or did not do caused them. She also detailed different types of autoimmune diseases – systemic and organ-specific – and explained how certain conditions such as Type 1 diabetes, Hashimoto’s, lupus , rheumatoid arthritis and Sjögren’s, among others, occurred. She also outlined the diagnostic procedures and described how treatment worked to calm the immune system, ease symptoms, and support the body.

Prabash Prabhakaran, director and senior consultant, neurology, SIMS Hospital, Chennai, explained that autoimmune conditions could affect any part of the nervous system, and the doctor’s first goal was to localise the affected area and understand which part of the nervous system was involved. This was followed by assessing the tempo: figuring out if the condition developed over hours, days, weeks, or longer. After this, a differential diagnosis was made, and supporting evidence was sought through tests, he explained. He stressed that antibody results were evidence, not a diagnosis. He detailed different autoimmune conditions that affected the nervous system, and also explained when and how treatment worked.

Audience questions ranged from why women were more prone to autoimmune conditions, whether or not stress played a role in their development, and understanding autoimmune conditions in children, to the latest treatment modalities. Both doctors noted that with increasing awareness, more people were seeking medical attention and receiving diagnoses for these conditions. They also said that a lot of research was ongoing and many new drugs and therapies had been introduced. They stressed the importance of not ignoring symptoms that lasted for more than a few weeks, and the need to seek medical help and start treatment early to ensure optimal management and a good quality of life.
The webinar video can be viewed at: https://www.youtube.com/live/7n871p7Cnjw?si=ttE95XRE_syPWSMM

articles.title: Night shift work related with differences in heart structure, heart muscle function: Study
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Published in the journal European Heart Journal-Cardiovascular Imaging, is the first large-scale study to combine detailed cardiac MRI with proteomic and metabolomic profiling in relation to night-shift work, says research
Frequently working night shifts could be linked with differences in heart structure and functioning of the heart muscle, a new study has found.
Researchers from Zhengzhou University People's Hospital in China also found differences in biomarkers linked to cardiovascular health.

They said the research, published in the journal European Heart Journal-Cardiovascular Imaging, is the first large-scale study to combine detailed cardiac MRI with proteomic and metabolomic profiling in relation to night-shift work.
Working night shifts is associated with an increased risk of cardiovascular disease and cardiovascular mortality.

While the reasons for the link are not fully understood, previous studies have shown that a repeated misalignment between the body's circadian rhythm and the normal sleep-wake schedule can affect metabolism, inflammation, blood pressure regulation, and vascular function.
Data of 42,671 men and women in the U.K. Biobank, with a mean age of 52 at baseline — of whom 1,322 reported frequent night-shift work — were analysed.

Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Imaging scans revealed people who frequently worked night shifts tended to have slightly thicker walls in the heart in relation to the size of the main pumping chamber, and somewhat smaller heart chambers.

There was also a subtle difference in a measure of how the heart muscle contracts, even as the researchers did not observe a significant difference in ejection fraction, a standard measure of the heart's overall pumping function.
The team said the differences they observed were small average differences at a population level and do not mean that all night-shift workers will develop heart disease or heart failure.

"Nonetheless, we suggest that people who regularly work at night should pay particular attention to looking after their cardiovascular health. That includes not smoking, staying physically active, maintaining a healthy diet and weight, getting sufficient sleep and keeping sleep timing as regular as possible, and keeping blood pressure, cholesterol, and blood glucose well controlled," author Dr. Muwei Li, from Zhengzhou University, said.

The study also found that frequent night-shift work was associated with differences in specific blood markers, such as lower levels of DHA, an omega-3 fatty acid that supports heart and blood vessel health.
Higher levels of markers relating to triglycerides, a type of fat that can raise the risk of heart disease when levels are too high, and markers relating to inflammation, were also found.

articles.title: Odisha worker allegedly forced into Russia-Ukraine war, family seeks rescue
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Maguni Sahu’s family alleges that agents duped the 35-year-old migrant worker from Ganjam into working for an armed organisation somewhere along the Russia-Ukraine border, and says it has been out of touch with him for five days
A migrant worker from Odisha’s Ganjam district was allegedly duped by agents and forced to work for an armed organisation in Russia, his family members said.

Identified as Maguni Sahu, 35, the worker had travelled to Russia about four months ago to work at an apple farm in Krasnodar. A resident of Mathura village under Khallikote block in Ganjam district, Mr. Sahu had worked at the farm for barely a month before he was allegedly deceived into working for an organisation believed to be linked to the Russian military.

“My maternal uncle, Maguni Sahu, was deceived by some agents in Russia. He has studied only up to Class X. He informed us that he was forced to work for an armed organisation, though he could not identify it. The only thing he could figure out was that he was working somewhere along the Russia-Ukraine border,” said his nephew, Deepak Pradhan, on Saturday (November 28, 2026).

Mr. Sahu’s family members have approached the Ganjam Collector and labour officials, seeking their intervention to secure his release and facilitate his return to India. articles.title: Kuvempu University Registrar denies allegations of irregularities in digital evaluation of answer scripts
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: R. Thimmarayappa, Registrar (Evaluation) of Kuvempu University, has stated that there were no irregularities in the digital evaluation of answer scripts and that the system was introduced as directed by the State government and that the necessary procedures were followed to select the service provider.

In a press release issued on Saturday, Prof. Thimmarayappa said the service provider was selected through all prescribed tender procedures on the Karnataka Public Procurement Portal (KPPP), and the rate quoted by the selected provider was much lower than the rates for comparable services at other universities.
The Registrar gave this clarification in view of press conference by a youth organisation alleging irregularities in the evaluation system.

He said, “Evaluation of four undergraduate examinations has already been completed successfully through the digital system. It also helped the university secure the NAAC ‘A’ grade. Digital evaluation is a transparent and efficient system, and no examination malpractice has taken place.”

Following allegations of financial burden on the university due to the introduction of the system, chartered accountants have been appointed, as per the decision of the University Syndicate, to conduct an examination. The audit of related income and expenditure is under way, he said.

Kuvempu University has adopted the Unified University and College Management System (UUCMS), as have other State universities, on the government’s directions. Student registration, examination applications, entry of course codes, examinations and attendance, enrolment, and uploading of internal marks are all done at the college level. Result problems caused by data-entry or upload errors are being rectified on a priority basis in coordination with the State UUCMS Centre, he said.

Admissions to PG and PhD programmes are being conducted transparently as per university rules. Admission, examination and evaluation fees have been fixed as per the relevant orders of the Higher Education Department of the Government of Karnataka, he added.

articles.title: Experts discuss advances in fistula treatment at international conference in Hyderabad
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Management of complex and recurrent fistulas, advances in surgical techniques and the need to minimise post-operative complications were among the issues discussed at the first international conference on fistula management, ‘FIX-Tula Congress 2026’, organised by Yashoda Hospitals, Secunderabad, in Hyderabad on Saturday.
The three-day conference, which began on Friday, brought together over 550 surgeons and other medical professionals from India and abroad.

Speaking at the conference, Yashoda Hospitals Director Pavan Gorukanti stressed the need for medical professionals to keep abreast of technological advancements and exchange knowledge and clinical experiences to improve treatment outcomes.

Senior Proctologist and organising chairperson of the conference Shanti Vardhani said accurate identification of the fistula tract through magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and endoanal ultrasound was essential for determining the appropriate treatment for each patient.

She said the primary objectives of fistula treatment were to control the disease, preserve the function of muscles responsible for bowel control, minimise post-operative complications and reduce the risk of recurrence. She also dwelt on various surgical techniques, including fistulotomy, laser treatment and video-assisted procedures.

Medical experts Phil Tozer from the United Kingdom, Giulio Santoro from Italy, Arun Rojanasakul from Thailand, Francis Seow-Choen from Singapore and Valentin Sojar from Slovenia shared their clinical experiences and discussed advances in fistula management.
Yashoda Hospitals, Secunderabad, Unit Head Vijay Kumar stressed the importance of specialised training programmes and workshops in enhancing surgical skills.
The conference, which concludes on Sunday, features live surgical demonstrations, scientific sessions and hands-on workshops.

articles.title: Kiran Bedi calls for special care leave for parents of children with disabilities
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: National Parents’ Meet begins at the All India Institute of Speech and Hearing in Mysuru

Former Puducherry Lieutenant Governor and retired IPS officer Kiran Bedi on Saturday suggested introducing a dedicated care leave provision for parents of children with disabilities to help them balance professional commitments with caregiving responsibilities.
“Just as maternity and paternity leave are provided, the government should consider introducing care leave for parents of children with special abilities,” she said.

Ms. Bedi was speaking after inaugurating the two-day 32nd National Parents’ Meet, organised by PARIVAAR, the National Confederation of Parent Organisations, in association with Maulana Azad National Urdu University, Hyderabad, and the All India Institute of Speech and Hearing (AIISH), on the AIISH premises here.

Emphasising the need for institutional support to families caring for children with disabilities, she said parents must participate in shaping policies and safeguarding the rights of persons with disabilities.
Ms. Bedi suggested the formation of awareness, advocacy and activism groups for supporting policy implementation and pursuing collective action.

She also called for greater involvement of fathers in caregiving, observing that the responsibility of raising children with disabilities should not rest entirely on mothers. Stressing the need for a change in societal attitudes, she said persons with disabilities must be treated with dignity and provided opportunities for independence, empowerment and inclusion.
In his address, PARIVAAR president Pankaj Maru said the organisation represented more than 300 parent and non-parent organisations across the country.

AIISH director Pushpavathi highlighted the institute’s contributions to rehabilitation and early intervention, while NIEPID director B.V. Ramkumar emphasised the importance of family-centred rehabilitation.
D.K. Menon and B. Elangovan, deputy director, technical education, JSS, were present.

The meet, themed “From Care to Empowerment: Building Inclusive Communities Through Strong Families and Collective Action”, will deliberate on how families, institutions and parent-led organisations can work together to promote the rights, self-advocacy and participation of persons with intellectual and developmental disabilities.
On the occasion, the Divyang SARTHI mobile application, designed to support learning among persons with intellectual and developmental disabilities, was launched.

articles.title: Union government’s focus on quantum technologies will benefit engineering students, says NSTL scientist
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Naval Science and Technological Laboratory (NSTL) Visakhapatnam scientist F.V. Shaji said on Saturday (November 28, 2026) that the Union government’s focus on quantum technologies would create new job opportunities and benefit students across the country. He attended the Global Qiskit Fall Fest as the guest of honour. The two-day event was organised at Satya Institute of Technology and Management (SITAM) in Vizianagaram.

He noted that quantum technologies are the need of the hour for research in the defence sector and urged youngsters to undertake internships and short-term courses on the country’s emerging technologies. articles.title: Develop branch mutts as educational hubs: Minister Satish Jarkiholi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Public Works Department Minister Satish Jarkiholi on Saturday urged the Valmiki community to utilise constitutional provisions, education, and government welfare schemes for socio-economic progress, while calling for branch mutts to be developed into centres of social, religious, and educational empowerment.

​Speaking after laying the foundation stone for the Valmiki Gurupeetha branch mutt and educational facilities, organised by the Rajanahalli Maharshi Valmiki Gurupeetha Trust at Bandolli village in Surpur taluk, Mr. Jarkiholi stressed the need to form local committees to oversee the development of these institutions.

Highlighting the State government’s commitment, the Minister said ₹5 crore had already been released for basic infrastructure at the Bandolli branch. “We plan to provide an additional grant of around ₹25 crore in phases through the Scheduled Tribes Welfare Department to establish hostels, schools, higher education institutions, and training centres,” he said.
Calling mutts permanent assets of society, he expressed confidence that the Bandolli branch would match the stature of the main mutt at Rajanahalli within five years.

​MP for Raichur G. Kumar Naik noted that despite its significant population, the community required sustained socio-economic uplift and stressed the need to continue the push for 7% reservation. He also advocated for a road bridge across the Krishna to improve connectivity between Lingsugur and Surpur.

​Former Minister Narasimha Naik (Raju Gowda) said the Kanaka Gurupeetha and Valmiki Peetha should function like the “two eyes” of the Sagaranadu region, urging leaders to set aside political differences to safeguard the 7% reservation.

​Rajanahalli Maharshi Valmiki Gurupeetha seer Jagadguru Prasannananda Mahaswami lauded the ₹25-crore initiative, noting that it would support the education and accommodation of nearly 1,000 children in the Kalyana Karnataka region. He felicitated Sujatha Venugopal Jewargi for providing land for the mutt at a concessional rate.

​Varadaneshwara Mahaswami of Golapalli, Scheduled Tribes Welfare Minister T. Raghumurthy, MLAs Raja Venugopal Naik, B. Devendrappa, Annapurna Tukaram, Anil Chikkamadu, and Channareddy Patil Tunnur, along with former MP B.V. Naik and former MLA Pratapgouda Patil, were present.

articles.title: ASHA workers to continue stir despite CM’s assurance of ₹2,000 honorarium hike
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Union says key demands remain unaddressed; indefinite agitation at Freedom Park to continue

Despite a meeting with Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar, who announced a ₹2,000 hike in their monthly honorarium from January 1, ASHA workers in Bengaluru decided to continue their indefinite strike stating that their key demands had remained unaddressed.

Though a delegation of workers appeared to have agreed to the government’s proposal during talks with the Chief Minister on Saturday, the Karnataka Rajya Samyuktha ASHA Karyakarteyara Sangha later decided to continue the agitation.

Union State president K. Somashekar and State secretary D. Nagalakshmi said the workers were dissatisfied with the offer and had expressed it in a meeting later in the day. Some even alleged that the leaders had agreed to withdraw without proper consultation with the workers. It was, therefore, decided that the protest would not stop until they get a written assurance on their demands.
The union launched an indefinite day-and-night protest at Freedom Park on November 17, demanding a fixed monthly honorarium of ₹15,000.

Its other demands include the release of pending incentives and retirement benefits, an end to compulsory mobile-based work or a separate incentive for it, and a special incentive of ₹5,000 for workers completing National Institute of Open Schooling (NIOS) training.
The union has also sought payment of honorarium and incentives for at least three months to workers undergoing treatment for serious illnesses.

Mr. Shivakumar announced the hike after discussions with ASHA workers’ representatives at Krishna, his official residence, on Saturday. Earlier, Health Minister U.T. Khader had also held talks with the protesting workers.

The revised honorarium will ensure a guaranteed monthly payment of ₹10,000 to more than 40,000 ASHA workers from January 1, in addition to performance-based incentives. The Chief Minister said the decision followed demands for a revision of the honorarium, which had remained unchanged for three years.

Explaining the funding arrangement under the National Health Mission (NHM), Mr. Khader said the Centre contributed ₹1,200 towards the fixed ₹2,000 component, while the State bore the remaining ₹800. The State also provides the entire ₹5,000 honorarium and contributes towards team-based and performance-based incentives.

According to the government, the State accounts for ₹7,000, or nearly 74%, of the existing monthly payments, while the Centre contributes ₹2,500, or 26%. Mr. Shivakumar said the Centre had not revised its fixed contribution since 2018-19 and urged it to increase its share.

Describing ASHA workers as an important part of the State’s healthcare system, he said the government had treated the protesters with respect and instructed the police to do the same. He also alleged that attempts had been made to politicise the agitation and divide the workers.

articles.title: Cybercrime takes a darker turn: Deepfakes, revenge and stalking fuel surge in online abuse
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Investigators report more than double the number of cases over the past year, as perpetrators weaponise intimate images, morphed content and AI-generated material to threaten, shame and control victims

Revenge, anger and personal vendetta are increasingly driving cyberstalking and technology-facilitated sexual offences, with Delhi Police investigators reporting at least a doubling of such cases over the past year. From former partners threatening to circulate intimate photographs to anonymous accounts using morphed images and artificial intelligence-generated deepfakes to target women, investigators are witnessing a shift towards more persistent and complex forms of online abuse.

The scale of the problem is also reflected in data from the National Cybercrime Reporting Portal (NCRP), which recorded a 118.4% increase in online crimes against women, from 22,188 cases in 2020 to 48,475 in 2024 over four broad categories of offences — online child sexual abuse and exploitation, gang rape and sexual abuse-related online content, sexually explicit acts and sexually obscene material. Delhi police officials said that cases of cyber stalking, technology-driven revenge crimes has at least doubled over the past year.

In a case involving a 17-year-old girl in Delhi, her digitally manipulated sexual images were found on several adult websites and intermediary file-hosting services. The girl’s 38-year-old aunt, a medical professional, approached the helpline after finding sexually explicit content bearing her niece’s facial features online.

Available timestamps suggested that the material had been online for some time before it was discovered, making it difficult to establish when it was first uploaded and identify those responsible. Following takedown requests through multiple channels, including the NCRP, 28 links were removed from hosting platforms within two weeks. The content was also digitally fingerprinted to reduce the possibility of it being uploaded again, though search thumbnails and indexed traces continued to surface.

In another case in Delhi, a woman was targeted by her son’s schoolmate, a Class 11 student, who used artificial intelligence to create morphed images and deepfakes of her. The content was uploaded on pornographic websites along with the woman’s phone number, a Delhi Police official said.
The accused was traced through his Instagram account, where he had also shared the content. The phone number was subsequently traced through the material circulated online, the official said.

In another case, a 23-year-old woman from Mumbai was threatened by her Delhi-based former partner after their two-and-a-half-year relationship ended. He threatened to circulate intimate photographs taken during their relationship unless she resumed contact with him.

Over the following months, the photographs were sent to members of her family and professional contacts. Her employment contract was not renewed. After a cybercrime complaint was closed without visible action, she attempted to end her life, but her family intervened.

A Zero FIR was registered in Mumbai in March 2025 and transferred to Delhi, where the accused was based. He later travelled to Mumbai and threw firecrackers through a window into the woman’s living room, where her siblings were sleeping. He was arrested the same day and remains in custody.

Meri Trustline, a helpline run by the Mumbai-based RATI Foundation for people facing online abuse and cyberbullying, has documented a growing volume of harmful content requiring intervention. According to data shared with The Hindu , between August 2024 and July 2025, it received 626 calls, of which 130 cases required active intervention. Across these cases, it recorded 253 categorised instances of online harm and reported 1,137 harmful links and accounts to social media platforms and other intermediaries, a 112% increase from 537 in the previous reporting period. Of these, 981 were taken down.

Women accounted for 68% of the 130 victim-survivors, while men made up 26%; the remaining 6% did not disclose their gender. Delhi accounted for 12 cases (9.2%), making it the third-largest location in the helpline’s caseload after Maharashtra (24.6%) and West Bengal (12.3%). Uttar Pradesh accounted for seven cases, Haryana four, Rajasthan three, Punjab two, Chandigarh two and Himachal Pradesh one.

The report found that 91 of the 130 perpetrators (70%) were unknown to the victim-survivors, while 39 (30%) were known to them. Of the known perpetrators, 36 were reported to be men. These cases often involved people who had prior access to private images or communications, with abuse linked to relationship breakdowns, betrayal of trust and attempts to retain control after separation.

Uttar Pradesh accounted for seven cases, Haryana four, Rajasthan three, Punjab two, Chandigarh two and Himachal Pradesh one.

articles.title: Changes in global garment sourcing trend to bring orders to Tiruppur
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Orders worth over ₹200 crore are said to have been shifted out of Bangladesh in November following labour unrest in that country, and a substantial part of it is expected to have come to India.
In Tiruppur, a major garment exporting cluster, exporters say it will take longer for the industries to benefit from diversion of orders from Bangladesh.

“Tiruppur should build its capacity to tap these opportunities,” said K.M. Subramanian, president of the Tiruppur Exporters Association (TEA). Large players are getting these orders now but are able to cater to the demands of the major brands, he added.

Raja Shanmugham, former president of the Association, said because of the disturbances in Bangladesh, and the good prospects of EU FTA coming into effect in the near future, several brands are starting to look for the right suppliers in India.
However, placement of orders will take place only in the coming months. The brands are exploring alternative sources now and the actual orders are likely to be finalised in March, he said.

Joint secretary of the TEA Kumar Duraiswamy explained that India’s trade agreements with the U.K. and the European Union in the last two years even as it negotiates a trade deal with the U.S. are throwing open opportunities for garment exporters. Global brands are looking at shifting their suppliers from China and Bangladesh for multiple reasons.

“Today, the dynamics of global sourcing are changing,” he said. Over the past year, these companies have been identifying new partners and upgrading existing production facilities to meet their specific requirements.

The U.S. continues to be a major destination for Indian exporters because the average annual spend of an American family in clothing and footwear ranges between $2,000 and $3,000, whereas it is just about $1,000 in the EU. Further, American buyers and brands are price conscious while the European brands look at compliances and audits.
While the U.S. will continue to be a major buyer of Indian garments despite the tariffs, several factories are also gearing up to meet the requirements of the EU buyers.
With the geopolitical developments affecting economies of many countries, European brands are also deferring taking delivery of the orders or cutting down on the orders across their supplier bases.

In the case of new suppliers, they are looking at a minimum 500 machines in a factory. Hence, while large companies are benefitting now from the orders diverted from Bangladesh, India SME factories should upgrade and work to tap these opportunities, he said.

articles.title: Congress pursuing politics of anarchy, coups to capture power: Rajnath Singh
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Singh said Congress leader Rahul Gandhi’s politics were not based on public issues but on creating a false narrative against Prime Minister Narendra Modi

Highlighting the impact of the “historic decision” to abrogate Article 370 in J&K, Union Defence Minister Rajnath Singh on Saturday (November 28, 2026) said the Congress was not respecting democracy “but pursuing the politics of anarchy and coups to capture power”.

“The Congress is maligning democracy, constitutional institutions and the Election Commission, spreading anarchy and tarnishing the country’s image for the sake of power,” said Mr. Singh, during the ‘ Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao ’ [’Save Democracy, End Anarchy’] Padyatra in Jammu.

Targeting Congress leader and Leader of Opposition (LoP) Rahul Gandhi , Mr. Singh said Mr. Gandhi’s politics were not based on public issues but on creating a false narrative against Prime Minister Narendra Modi .

“Blaming EVMs [Electronic Voting Machines] or the Election Commission for electoral defeats has become a habit of the Congress. Rahul Gandhi makes allegations but has no evidence to support them. He challenges Prime Minister Narendra Modi Ji, but his participation in the Parliament on public issues remains below the national average of Member of Parliaments,” said Mr. Singh.

Referring to the recent summit organised by the Congress in Hyderabad, Mr. Singh said, “At the summit, in the presence of Rahul Gandhi, an Italian leader had raised the slogan of ‘ Vote Chor, Gaddi Chhod ’ [’Vote thief, leave the throne’]. Such actions are unacceptable to the self-respecting people of India. The people of India would never tolerate calls for coups and regime change through the creation of anarchy in any healthy democratic system.”

Terming the abrogation of Article 370 in 2019 as a “historic decision”, Mr. Singh said, “Under the leadership of PM Modi Ji, J&K has witnessed expansion in development, tourism and healthcare facilities. J&K holds a special place in the political journey of the Bharatiya Janata Party.”

“It is the very land where Sher-e-Duggar Pandit Prem Nath Dogra dedicated his entire life to the complete integration of J&K with India. Dr. Syama Prasad Mookerjee also raised the slogan of ‘One Nation, One Constitution and One Flag' from this very land. J&K’s accession to India was not merely the integration of a geographical region; rather, it represented the nation’s resolve to preserve the soul, identity, unity and integrity of India,” he said.

He said J&K, in the past, was treated as separate from the rest of India. “Even the President of India was once called a ‘Non-State Subject’ by a Tehsildar during a land registration process. The BJP resolved to eliminate terrorism and has achieved considerable success in this regard,” said Mr. Singh.

Quoting a Kashmiri proverb, “Patim Mashrav, Bronṭh Kun Nazar Thav” [Forget the past, look ahead], Mr. Singh said, “After 2019, the people of J&K received their rights, separatism is declining, and the path towards making Jammu and Kashmir a developed state has been cleared”.

articles.title: Airstrike on Myanmar wedding venue kills around 20, say witnesses
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Myanmar has been in the throes of civil war since a coup deposed Aung San Suu Kyi's elected government in 2021, and monitoring group ACLED says more than 100,000 people have been killed on all sides
Around 20 people were killed when a Myanmar military airstrike hit a wedding venue in a conflict area on Saturday, witnesses said, the second mass casualty incident in the country in three days.

Videos taken by one witness, which AFP was not able to verify independently, showed bloodied victims being taken away for treatment after the strike in a village in Moe Bye, an area on the borders of Shan and Karenni states with large numbers of internally displaced people.
The leader of a rescue organisation put the toll at 21, including five children.
Myanmar has been in the throes of civil war since a coup deposed Aung San Suu Kyi's elected government in 2021, and monitoring group ACLED says more than 100,000 people have been killed on all sides.
The military controls Moe Bye town, but opposition forces operate in villages and rural areas outside it.
"I heard the sound of aircraft flying nearby, but I thought they would not bomb our area," the witness, who asked not to be identified, told AFP.
He went into his house, and "then I heard a bomb blast and saw lots of smoke where the airstrike hit", he said.
The bomb struck a wedding venue where preparations were being made for two displaced people to marry, he said.
He rushed to the scene to try to help. "I found 17 dead bodies" and many wounded, he said.
"I was shocked and didn't know who to rescue first. But one wounded woman told me to get children out first.
"There are some people missing, including my niece," he said. "I haven't been able to find her yet."
It was not possible to contact the Myanmar military for comment about the strike, or another in a different area two days earlier.

articles.title: Sri Lanka appoints parliamentary panel to study 1983 anti-Tamil riots
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Around 3,000 Tamils were killed between July 23 and July 30, 1983, in riots, also known as the ‘Black July’ riots, across the country
Sri Lanka has appointed a parliamentary panel to study the 1983 anti-Tamil riots and their impact, Speaker Jagath Wickremaratna said on Saturday (November 28, 2026).

articles.title: Bangladesh deploys border guards across seven districts amid political unrest, says report
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: As many as 56 platoons have been deployed in Gopalganj, Hasina's home district, according to a report on the state-run BSS news agency

Bangladesh has deployed border guard personnel across seven districts amid heightened political tensions over ousted Prime minister Sheikh Hasina's planned return to the country, according to a local media report.
As many as 56 platoons have been deployed in Gopalganj, Hasina's home district, according to a report on the state-run BSS news agency.
The deployment comes amid unrest involving clashes, crude bomb blasts and arson attacks reported in recent weeks as Hasina's planned return on December 16 has become a source of political tension.
The attacks were blamed on supporters of her activities-banned Awami League, while the government accused party leaders abroad of inciting violence.

Hasina, who has been living in India since fleeing Bangladesh in August 2024, has said she plans to return on December 16, the day Bangladesh celebrates its victory over Pakistan in the 1971 Liberation War.
The BSS report, quoting a Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) press release, said 120 platoons had been deployed across Dhaka, Gazipur, Narayanganj, Mymensingh, Gopalganj, Chattogram and Cox's Bazar.

According to the breakdown, 17 platoons have been deployed in Savar and Ashulia in Dhaka district, 19 in Gazipur, seven in Narayanganj, two in Bhaluka in Mymensingh, 56 in Gopalganj, eight in Chattogram and seven in Cox's Bazar, among other areas.

The BGB personnel are operating in coordination with the respective district administrations and other law enforcement agencies, following directives from Bangladesh's Ministry of Home Affairs, the report said.
They are tasked with strengthening security and surveillance at key installations, industrial zones and other important locations, as well as preventing unrest and violence.
The BGB headquarters is also monitoring live footage from drones, body-worn cameras and other surveillance equipment to coordinate operations on the ground, it added.
Hasina has been living in India since fleeing Bangladesh on August 5, 2024, following a student-led uprising that toppled her 15-year government.
In November 2025, Hasina was sentenced to death in absentia for crimes against humanity over the 2024 crackdown on protesters. Hasina has refused the allegations.

articles.title: ISRO invites Indian industry to develop human spaceflight analog simulation facility
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The Bengaluru-based HSFC has issued an Expression of Interest in this regard on November 26, 2026.

ISRO’s Human Space Flight Centre (HSFC) has invited the Indian industry for the complete execution of the Mission ANTARIKSH which is the country’s Earth-based Human Spaceflight Analog Simulation Facility.
The Bengaluru-based HSFC has issued an Expression of Interest (EoI) in this regard on November 26, 2026.
The facility is intended for crew training, mission rehearsal, evaluation of systems and validation of operational procedures.

It will also comprise representative spacecraft and space station modules, mission control centre, simulation hardware and software and associated support infrastructure for the conduct of human spaceflight analog missions.
India, apart from the ongoing Gaganyaan mission, is also looking to have its own operational space station, the Bharatiya Antariksh Station (BAS) by 2035 and launch the crewed lunar mission by 2040.

According to the EoI, the scope of work includes design, development, procurement, fabrication, assembly, deployment, integration, testing and commissioning of the facility and its systems, followed by operation, maintenance and management of the specified mission campaigns.

Apart from end-to-end realisation of the facility, the Indian industry, either individually or through a consortium, will also be entrusted in the mission operations and inter-mission maintenance of the facility for a period of two years.

The EoI states that the facility will comprise representative Gaganyaan and BAS simulator modules, a Mission Control Centre, a Neutral Buoyancy Simulator, specialised Space Specific Engineering Task (SsET) systems, and associated crew, medical, ground support and utility infrastructure.

“These facilities shall support simulation of selected human spaceflight activities, including operations within the modules, extravehicular activities, docking, robotic operations, crew coordination and contingency response. The hardware and software shall be integrated to support Human-in-theLoop (HITL) and Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) simulations under controlled terrestrial conditions,” the EoI states.

The quantum of work includes establishment of an Mission ANTARIKSH simulation facility which can suppor the conduct of six analog mission campaigns in two operational phases, with three campaigns per phase, preceded by a preparatory dry rehearsal.
During the execution of the project, the HSFC through a committee will monitor the progress of the facility build-up and the subsequent conduct of mission campaigns.

Mr. Netanyahu said in a statement that he should ⁠lead the Israeli government but “given the magnitude of ⁠the existential threat and the possibility that a government could be formed that isn’t ‌able to deal with this danger,” his “responsibility as a leader” required he “put everything ​aside.”

articles.title: Hakeem Jeffries | History maker
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The New York Congressman, set to become the first Black Speaker of the U.S. House, faces the challenge of holding a diverse party together while navigating the Trump presidency

Democrats in the U.S. House of Representatives have nominated Hakeem Jeffries, a Representative from New York, for Speaker. In the November 3 midterm elections, the Democratic Party won 259 seats in the 435-member House, while President Donald Trump’s Republican Party secured 173. Democrats also wrested control of the Senate from the Republicans. Once formally elected Speaker on January 3, Mr. Jeffries would become the first Black lawmaker to lead the chamber. Mr. Jeffries, who has served as the House Minority Leader since 2023, was re-elected as the party leader in a 251-11 secret-ballot vote last week. The vote is “a high honour and a distinct privilege”, he said.

Born in 1970 in Brooklyn, New York, Mr. Jeffries is the son of a social worker and family welfare counsellor. After attending several state schools, he opted to study political science at the State University of New York, Binghamton. Reports say that during his final year at university, he was inspired to enter politics after the acquittal of the police officers who beat African American Rodney King, following which there was widespread rioting in Los Angeles. Nevertheless, post law school, Mr. Jeffries signed up to work with one of New York’s top law firms and then went on to serve as an in-house litigator for CBS and Viacom.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Piracy has seen a resurgence in the waters off the Horn of Africa, with at least 16 attacks since April, the highest level since 2013

Pirates from Somalia briefly hijacked a UAE-based ship off Yemen after disguising themselves as fishermen and hiding among Yemen's Somali community, security officials and a maritime monitor said Saturday.
Piracy has seen a resurgence in the waters off the Horn of Africa, with at least 16 attacks since April, the highest level since 2013.
British maritime agency UKMTO said assailants had boarded a cargo ship some 120 kilometres (70 miles) southwest of the Yemeni port of Balhaf.
It said later in the day that the pirates had "vacated the vessel", which was proceeding to its next port of call.
According to security officials in the Somali state of Puntland, where the main network of pirates is based, the vessel was the MV Marsa Virgo.
It is owned by Marsa Ocean Shipping, based in the United Arab Emirates, and operates under the Panama flag.
The attack was carried out by six Somali gunmen who left Puntland in a fishing boat and crossed the Gulf of Aden to Yemen, the three security officials told AFP.
They tracked the gunmen's movements via sources in the Somali community and spoke to AFP on condition of anonymity.
They said the six assailants embedded with Somalis living in southern Yemen and accessed weapons through them.
This was the first time an attack had been conducted by Somali pirates from Yemeni territory, they said.
One official said it was wrong to blame the Houthis, the Iran-backed Yemeni group that controls the Red Sea coastline, for facilitating piracy in the region.

"Everyone brings up the Houthis when it comes to why Somali pirates continue to hijack ships off the coast of Yemen, but in reality it's rogue criminal elements within the local Somali refugee community assisting the pirates in Puntland," the official said.

articles.title: Taipei mayor re-elected in tight race
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Chiang Wan-an, 47, is a rising star in the Kuomintang party (KMT), which favours closer relations with China, and is seen as a potential future presidential candidate
Taipei Mayor Chiang Wan-an was re-elected on Saturday (November 28, 2026) after a nail-biting race against China critic Puma Shen in local elections held across the island democracy.
Mr. Chiang, 47, is a rising star in the Kuomintang party (KMT), which favours closer relations with China, and is seen as a potential future presidential candidate.
Mr. Shen, 44, was the underdog in the race for Taipei, which has long been a traditional KMT stronghold in northern Taiwan.
After winning easily four years ago, Mr. Chiang faced a tougher contest against Mr. Shen, who was seeking to become the capital's first Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) mayor in nearly 30 years.
Voter surveys in the weeks leading up to election day showed Mr. Shen closing in on Mr. Chiang, or even slightly ahead of his rival.
Mr.Shen stood in front of thousands of supporters, some of them crying, less than four hours after polling stations closed to concede defeat in the race that has gripped the island.
"The result is already out, I lost," Mr. Shen told the crowd.
Mr. Chiang went on stage a short time later, and thanked "legislator Mr. Shen and his supporters".
"Together, we have made this a celebration of democracy," Mr. Chiang told the audience.
Mr. Shen, a criminologist and former civil defence activist, became a lawmaker in 2024 and was an outspoken critic of Chinese interference operations against Taiwan.
He was accused by Beijing of being a "separatist" and barred from entering the country.
China claims Taiwan is part of its territory and has threatened to use force to annex the island.

articles.title: Fatal disagreement: on the COP31 summit
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Developed nations must bear much of the cost of carbon emissions

COP31 ended in Antalya, Türkiye, with a whimper. The 190-odd countries that had convened for nearly 12 days — a close to 50-hour overshoot — failed to agree on an overarching political statement , called a cover text, that acts as a stepping stone to future, collective global action on climate change. Usually, cover texts evolve as a final synthesis of deliberations ; the COP31 leadership, helmed by Türkiye and Australia, thought it fit to push for a cover text early in the proceedings. The headline sought was a global electrification target: 35% of global final energy consumption will come from electricity by 2035, in the hope that this would reduce direct fossil fuel emissions. Ultimately, the cover text failed to pass muster because the European Union objected to the text’s lack of any explicit mention of ‘fossil fuel,’ let alone its phase-out. The COP process is arduously protracted as even a single country’s objection can stall progress. Country-blocks outside the EU, such as coalitions of the least developed countries, island nations, some South American countries — reportedly 130 countries — were also insistent on fossil fuel language. While COP 31 made some progress on old pathways, such as the Just Transition agreement, it is perplexing that the delegations could not make progress on the other big prong of negotiations: climate finance.

The increase in solar panel installations and the significant shift towards battery use in grid storage and transport did not come cheap: the cost of the land required for their installation, their intermittent nature of being dependent on weather, grid upgrades all carry costs. It is global markets, imperfectly connected, but connected, that have managed to bring it to this stage over decades. India and China, major fossil emitters, with large, still indigent populations, are also leaders in total clean energy installations. Therefore it stands to reason that developed countries, which have committed to providing climate finance in recognition of their historical emissions, make good on past promises to shoulder the cost of the carbon emissions that are responsible for warming. Economic crises are a feature, and not a bug, of the interconnected financial system enveloping the world and there are, undeniably, challenges to diverting the necessary finance towards countries most vulnerable to climate change impact. However, it is no longer prudent to sweep this under the rug by scuttling experimental approaches — namely carbon capture — as inimical to the broader commitment to eschew fossil fuel. When the primary framework climate agreement was crafted three decades ago, nobody envisaged AI and the drain that data centres portended or the wars that would see the vociferous antagonists of coal immediately shore up their gas reserves. Without honest good-faith dialogue, the COP is at risk of being a sideshow: a mortal blow to multilateralism.

articles.title: Just verdict: on Myanmar and the International Court of Justice
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Rohingya cannot return unless Myanmar turns democratic

On November 19, the International Court of Justice held that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya. It is for the first time that the court has found any state responsible for the crime. The verdict, with nine votes to six, was not lightly reached. Genocide requires proof of an intent to destroy a group. In the absence of direct evidence of a plan, the court could infer that intent only if it was “the only reasonable inference” from the facts, a high bar to affix responsibility. The facts it accepted are harrowing. In 2017, in what Myanmar’s army called “clearance operations” against the insurgent Arakan Rohingya Salvation Army, at least 10,000 Rohingya were killed, 1,834 raped and 392 villages destroyed in northern Rakhine State. Over 7,00,000 fled to Bangladesh. Then Army chief Min Aung Hlaing, now Myanmar’s “civilian” President, called the “Bengali problem” an “unfinished job”. Myanmar argued that it had only been fighting insurgents or at worst, driving the Rohingya out or punishing them. The court said that the army drew no distinction between fighters and civilians, had no plan to move anyone, fired on fleeing people and killed children on a scale that could not be explained as punishment. Seen alongside decades of discrimination, the evidence pointed to an intent to destroy.

The incidents of 2017 were no aberration. The army drove lakhs of Rohingya into Bangladesh in 1978 and 1991-92. The junta stripped the Rohingya of citizenship in 1982 and the state branded them as “foreigners” in Arakan, disenfranchising them in 2015. While the junta’s Bamar-Buddhist vision has oppressed every minority, the Rohingya have been subjected to the most brutality. More than 1.2 million are in Bangladesh, living in dilapidated conditions, made worse due to diminished international aid. The court ordered Myanmar to allow their safe, voluntary and dignified return and to compensate them, but it has no means of enforcing its judgment. Only the UN Security Council can, but it will be subject to vetoes by Myanmar’s backers, China and Russia. On the very day of the verdict, the two joined the U.S. in Shenzhen to declare the “immunities of State officials” of “paramount importance”. Others, India among them, have courted the regime in Naypyitaw regardless, following sham elections that made the junta leader civilian President earlier this year. And Rakhine State, mired in civil war, is now mostly held by the Arakan Army which is accused of atrocities against the Rohingya. Only a truly democratic, federal, plural and peaceful Myanmar can bring the Rohingya home in safety.

articles.title: Pressure tactics: On the new U.S. tariffs on India
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The new U.S. tariffs must not erode India’s stand on a trade deal

The latest U.S. tariffs on India are nothing more than a pressure tactic to push for the signing of a trade deal. The U.S. Trade Representative (USTR) has proposed to levy a tariff of 25% for India’s apparent use of strategic excess manufacturing capacity to the detriment of American industry. This is the second-highest tariff rate the USTR has applied across the 14 countries that it has taken action against. The pressure on India does not come from the 25% rate but from the 17% this could be reduced to if it signs a trade deal with the U.S. This latest action is yet another example of how, despite the frothiness of India-U.S. trade relations over the past year and a half, the actual substance has not changed. The 25% rate now proposed, which is net of existing tariffs, is nearly the same as the 26% rate that U.S. President Donald Trump had first announced when he unveiled his ‘Liberation Day’ reciprocal tariffs in April 2025. Indeed, it is exactly the same as the 25% tariff he finally imposed in July 2025, before he imposed an additional 25% for India’s Russian oil imports. The 17% rate is also only marginally lower than the 18% that the two countries had agreed on in their joint statement in February 2026. It is also just one percentage point lower than the tariffs on competitors such as Indonesia and Malaysia. The allegation of India having excess capacity does not hold water. Indeed, were India to have excess manufacturing capacity in any sector, it would be the Government of India that would be the first to announce it with great fanfare, instead of denying it as it did. After all, that has been its aim since 2014.

Yet, even a basic assessment of India’s import dependence and the fact that manufacturing’s share in GDP is lower now than a decade ago shows that India is far from having excess manufacturing capacity in any sector. Further, higher tariffs are unlikely to reduce America’s imports of the goods from India that it does depend on. The USTR mentioned generic pharmaceuticals, telecommunication equipment, and renewable energy goods. The first two are items that India has developed expertise in, which is distinct from strategic excess capacity. A relatively small tariff disadvantage will not substantially erode the attractiveness of these Indian products. Renewable energy imports from India have swelled because the U.S. is reducing its purchases from China. Hanging over all of this are the 100% tariffs related to the purchase of Russian oil, which have only temporarily been paused. India has so far held off on signing a deal, and must go ahead with one only if it is convinced that the benefits at least equal the costs.

articles.title: Indefensible defiance: On Tamil Nadu and Court’s Thirupparankundram order
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Tamil Nadu should have followed Court order without backing Deepathoon claim

By defying the Supreme Court’s one-time direction to also light the ceremonial Karthigai Deepam at a stone pillar , claimed by Hindu groups to be a Deepathoon, atop the Thirupparankundram hills, the Tamil Nadu government has disregarded a constitutional body’s authority. Believed to be Lord Murugan’s first abode, the hills have, for centuries , witnessed an intersection of religious faiths, with occasional skirmishes leading to tense flare-ups and legal battles. They house the Arulmigu Subramaniya Swamy, Uchchi Pillaiyar and Kashi Viswanathar temples; Sultan Sikkandar Avulia Dargah; and also Jain beds. Historically, the lamp is lit near the Pillaiyar temple. In 1994-95, the Hindu Munnani precipitated matters, claiming that the moksha deepam (for departed souls) and Karthigai Deepam were being lit at the same place. It demanded the lamp be lit at a pillar, 50 metres from the Dargah. In multiple legal battles, successive governments, backed by hereditary priests (Sthaneeka Bhattars) , opposed the demand. Even in 1862 and 1912, courts had disallowed lamp lighting near the Dargah. The BJP and its affiliates have, since, aggressively weaponised the demand in the name of Hindu religious rights.

Against this backdrop, last year, the Madras High Cour t’s Madurai Bench, relying on the 1931 Privy Council ruling on ownership of the hills, held that “for the sake of protecting its property, the [Subramania Swamy] temple management is obliged to light the festival lamp at the Deepathoon” . The DMK government defied the order. Later, a Division Bench upheld the verdict. While staying this order recently, the Supreme Court cited the festival’s proximity to permit the lamp to be lit at the Deepathoon this year alone , clarifying that this did not constitute “essential religious practice”. The State filed a review petition , arguing when no right is recognised prima facie, a direction altering the existing position lacks judicial foundation. On Karthigai Deepam day, November 24, with the review pending, the government walked a tightrope. The Collector assured the High Court of compliance. Yet, the lamp was lit only at the traditional spot . The Collector has now apologised to the Court, blaming the temple’s Board of Trustees for not authorising the proposed lighting team at the Deepathoon. The administration has thus attempted to distinguish its proclaimed intent to comply with judicial directions from customs governed by the trustees. But it remains exposed to the charge of colluding with the temple authorities to breach a judicial mandate. The Deepathoon may be a mischievous prop deployed by self-serving Hindu groups, but the pillar stands on temple property. The State could have permitted the limited lighting, leaving the onus on the Court, without endorsing the Deepathoon claim or compromising religious amity. A democracy can remain healthy only when its constitutional pillars do not collide with one another.

articles.title: Cultural values of language remain irreplaceable in AI era: Arabic meet
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Artificial Intelligence (AI) may transform the way Arabic is learned and used, but human emotions and traditional values remain beyond the reach of technology, an international conference on the Arabic language held at Anvarul Islam Arabic College, Kuniyil, observed on Thursday.

The two-day conference, titled ‘Digital humanities: reimagining Arabic language and literature’, was organised by the Arabic department of the college in association with Calicut University’s Arabic department, Kerala State Higher Education Council, and Arab Union of Internet Writers.
Liyaqat Ali, deputy director of collegiate education, inaugurated the conference on Wednesday. College Principal K. Mohammed Fawaz presided over the function.
Liyaqat Ali, deputy director of collegiate education, inaugurating an international conference on Arabic at Anvarul Islam Arabic College, Kuniyil, on Wednesday. | Photo Credit: SAKEER HUSSAIN

Arabic scholars Sumayya Ibrahim Abu Thailath from Palestine, Najeeb Ali Mulkhath from Yemen, Simi K. Salim, K. Ali Noufal, I.P. Abdul Salam, C.M. Sabir Navas, K.A. Nasser, P. Firoz, M.K. Ameer Swalahi, Shakir Babu Kuniyil, and K.P. Abdul Haleem Thangal spoke.
E.T. Mohammed Basheer, MP, inaugurated the valedictory function on Thursday. He highlighted the growing global significance of the Arabic language in an increasingly interconnected world.
Scholars Mujeeb Nellikkuth, Ali Jafar, Mohammed Aman K., P. Sulaiman and C. Abdul Wahab spoke.

articles.title: BDO issues residence certificate to mother of child denied birth certificate due to SIR row
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Amina Khatun and Abdul Habib were denied a residence proof necessary for birth certificate on grounds that Abdul Habib’s name was struck off electoral rolls during SIR.

The district administration of Coochbehar district in West Bengal on Thursday (November 26, 2026) issued a residence certificate to the mother of a two-month-old infant, after her parents faced challenges to get the certificate on the ground that the name of the father was deleted from electoral rolls during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) held earlier this year.

The Hindu reported on November 25 that the birth certificate was denied to the infant because the father's name was deleted from the electoral roll during SIR. Amina Khatun, wife of Abdul Habib, gave birth to a girl at Dinhata Sub-Divisional Hospital on September 9. Amina Khatun and Abdul Habib approached the hospital and the concerned panchayat office to obtain their daughter’s birth certificate. The couple was reportedly asked to arrange residential verification from the local panchayat pradhan or MLA.

On the grounds that the name of Abdul Habib was deleted from the electoral roll in the SIR, the local BJP MLA office refused to give them residence proof. On Thursday (November 26), the BDO office issued a residence certificate to Amina Khatun.

“This is to certify that Amina Khatun, wife of Abdul Habib, is a permanent resident of village Khatamari P.O. Khatamari as per the enquiry report of Chowdhurihat Gram Panchayat -. Under Dinhata-II Development Block, P.S.: Sahebganj, Dist.: Cooch Behar. The name of the applicant has been enrolled in the Electoral Roll vide Part-191, Sl. No .848 of 7 Dinhata Assembly Constituency. I wish him/her all success in his/her life,” read the certificate issued by the BDO on Thursday.

Abdul Hamid told this correspondent that government officials came to his residence and took him to the BDO office where the residence proof was given to him. “I have received my residence verification certificate which I am going to submit at the hospital tomorrow. Hopefully, my daughter will now get the birth certificate soon,” the father said.

There have been allegations of denial of services by the West Bengal government to citizens whose names have been deleted from the electoral rolls during SIR. The Supreme Court, which oversaw the SIR process in the State, had made it clear that removal of a name from the electoral roll cannot be grounds for denial of services. The names of about 36 lakh electors deleted during SIR are pending before SIR tribunals in the State.

articles.title: Karnataka Industries Minister holds talks with four Japanese companies
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Large and Medium Industries Minister M.B. Patil held discussions with four Japanese companies, the fourth day of his visit to Japan, focusing on their existing operations in Karnataka and expansion plans

Large and Medium Industries Minister M.B. Patil held discussions with four Japanese companies on Thursday, the fourth day of his visit to Japan, focusing on their existing operations in Karnataka and expansion plans.

According to a release, during a meeting with Seiren Co. Ltd., a manufacturer of automotive interior materials, discussions focused on its manufacturing operations at the Kadakola Industrial Area in Mysuru and its plans to expand its presence in line with Toyota’s growing capacity in the State.

At a meeting with the leadership of Enomoto Co. Ltd., a Japanese manufacturer of precision connector components and semiconductor lead frames, discussions centred on potential expansion locations, including the Tumakuru Machine Tool Park and the Chennai-Bengaluru Industrial Corridor.

In a meeting with representatives of Secom and Toyota Tsusho Corporation, the Minister discussed the growth plans of Sakra World Hospital. Discussions were also held with Makino, a leading manufacturer of high-precision machine tools, the release said.
