articles.title: Amended Delimitation Bill likely to be tabled in special Parliament sitting from November 30
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Centre announces special sitting of Parliament from November 30, 2026, over 100 days since both Houses were adjourned without prorogation; government trying to pass the Bill after ‘operation lotus’, says Congress
The government has called for a special sitting of Parliament beginning Monday (November 30, 2026), where it is likely to table an amended Delimitation Bill.

The two Houses will meet on separate dates, Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju announced on Thursday (November 26, 2026), which is the 104th day since the Monsoon Session adjourned indefinitely on August 13.

Lok Sabha sittings will begin on November 30 and Rajya Sabha sittings on December 2. Both Houses will conclude on December 3. The last record of a session of Parliament continuing unprorogued was in 2008 , when it went on for 87 days.

The Union Cabinet will meet on Friday (November 27, 2026) to clear the amended legislation. According to sources, three crucial changes are being introduced: a uniform 50% increase in the share of Lok Sabha seats; extending the freeze for 25 years on using the 1971 Census as the basis to determine the proportional strength of each State in the Lok Sabha; and third, using the 2011 Census for redrawing constituencies within each State. This replicates the formula brought by the Atal Bihari Vajpayee government in the Constitution (Eighty-fourth Amendment) Act, 2001.

Reacting to the announcement, Congress general secretary (communication) Jairam Ramesh said the Narendra Modi government announced the session “after 105 days of operation lotus” in the hope of getting a “super-tainted” two-thirds majority to get the Bill passed. “Can there be a great insult to and assault on the Constitution,” he asked in a post on X, noting that the announcement came on Constitution Day.
Congress general secretary (organisation) K.C. Venugopal took to X to describe the attempt to pass the Delimitation Bill as “ sansad chori” .
“To orchestrate this murder of the Constitution on Constitution Day shows how badly they want to mock our precious democratic system. We will not allow this to pass,” Mr. Venugopal said.

Since April, when the legislative package, including the Delimitation Bill, was defeated by a united Opposition in the Lok Sabha, the seat arithmetic in the House has changed. Twenty TMC MPs broke away and merged with the Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI), pledging support to the NDA. TMC challenged the split, which is currently under Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla’s review. The NCPI faction, on Tuesday (November 24, 2026), 84 days after TMC’s challenge, submitted replies to Mr. Birla, defending its decision and asserting that the move did not violate any parliamentary or constitutional provisions.

Six Shiv Sena (UBT) MPs joined the Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena. Following the recent alliance between the BJP and the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD), the lone SAD MP is also expected to vote with the government. It is also learnt that the YSR Congress, which has four MPs in the Lok Sabha, will extend support to the government on the Bill.
In this evolving situation, all eyes are on the DMK, with 22 Lok Sabha MPs, and the NCP (Sharadchandra Pawar), with eight.
Senior NCP (SP) leader Supriya Sule, on Thursday (November 26, 2026), told reporters that pre-emptively opposing the law before its draft was made public was not a good move.

“First let the bill come. Let the entire bill come into our hands. When the bill is in our hands, then we will all talk about it, and if the bill is good for the nation, we might support it,” she said. She further added that there have been instances in the past when the Opposition has supported the government on matters of national importance and key reforms.

articles.title: Sthaneeka Bhattars make contradictory statements on the lighting of deepam
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes

But a letter purportedly written by the Bhattars, stating that they had not given any letter of consent, went viral on social media the next day

The Sthaneeka Bhattars of the Subramaniya Swamy Temple at Thirupparankundram gave some tense moments to the Madurai district administration by making contradictory statements on their “consent” for lighting the ceremonial lamp at the traditional spot — Deepa Mandapam — on Karthigai Deepam day.
Editorial | Indefensible defiance: On Tamil Nadu and Court’s Thirupparankundram order

The administration had submitted at the Supreme Court that despite its readiness to light the lamp at the deepathoon , it could not comply with the court directive as the temple’s Board of Trustees insisted on lighting the lamp only at the Deepa Mandapam, following age-old practices, customs and rituals, and agama rules.

A statement made on November 24 by the temple’s Executive Officer, G. Selvi, had said the reasoning for lighting the lamp at the Deepa Mandapam was backed by the Bhattars. However, the next day, a letter purportedly written by the Bhattars, stating that they had not given any letter of consent on lighting the lamp on November 24, went viral on social media. They said they had given consent for lighting the lamp at the usual spot near Uchipillaiyar Temple “last year” (2025). The recent statement by the Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Department referring to their consent, made “without consulting” them, had caused mental agony, they said.

Meanwhile, there was commotion outside the house of Swaminatha Bhattar late in the evening on Wednesday, as functionaries of the BJP and Hindu outfits arrived at the priest’s house. Temple officials too were present at the house. The BJP functionaries said the Bhattars were being “forced” to give a new letter of consent to help the officials substantiate their stand before the Supreme Court. The demonstrators were detained by the police.

An official of the Department said the Bhattars gave the new letter on Wednesday to the Board of Trustees. “The lighting of Karthigai Deepam has been done at the Uchipillaiyar Temple since 1996 with the cooperation of the temple authorities,” said the letter, signed by four Bhattars. However, they underlined that they were only replying to a letter written by the temple administration, seeking their opinion on this issue.

They reasoned that the Utchipillaiyar Temple, the Rajagopuram, and the venue for burning chokkapanai near the 16-Pillar Mandapam lie on a straight line, and the Utchipillaiyar Temple was located right above the sanctum sanctorum. They also confirmed that they had given the same opinion “in writing” on November 7, 2013 and December 4, 2025. “The deepam is lit at the deepamandapam after getting oral or written opinion from us every year. This is in line with the agama rules and age-old Saiva customs,” they clarified.

articles.title: In Rajasthan, the girls who refuse to be spoken for
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Rajasthan ranks sixth among India’s States with the highest prevalence of child marriage, according to the latest National Family Health Survey (2023-24). Poverty, the lack of education, and entrenched customs such as atta-satta, reinforced by a skewed sex ratio, continue to fuel the practice, particularly in tribal and rural areas. Now, a growing number of girls, empowered by education and greater access to social media, are saying no, reports Ashok Kumar. Meanwhile, the United Nations has declared November 27 as the International Day for the Elimination of Child, Early and Forced Marriage

Nandini (name changed), 16, who lives in Rajasthan’s Sikar, had mapped out her future: finish school, go to college, and get a job to be financially independent. Her family, however, had other plans. Last month, they fixed her wedding without her consent. But the Class 12 student refused to surrender her dreams. She picked up her father’s mobile phone and called the 24x7 child helpline, 1098.

Over the next few days, Nandini called the helpline more than six times, using whatever phone she could lay her hands on. Sometimes, she pretended she wanted to speak to her prospective groom; at other times, she sought to contact her friends. But each call carried an urgent message: wedding preparations were under way, guests were being invited, and the date was drawing closer. Help!

Each time, the call was connecting to the District Child Protection Office. “She had asked us not to contact her. She said she would call whenever she got a chance. Her first call came just three days before the wedding,” recalls Gargi Sharma, District Child Protection Officer.

With barely 72 hours to act, the team secured an injunction order from the court and stopped the wedding. The family was taken by surprise when officials arrived, suspecting that a neighbour had tipped them off. They never imagined that the quiet schoolgirl in their midst had been orchestrating her own rescue. Her identity as the whistleblower remained a secret.

The Sikar administration prevented 29 child marriages in 2024 and 10 in 2025. “In 2026, we have received information about 21 cases so far,” Sharma says. But there are many Nandinis, especially in India’s villages, who do not have the education or the agency to say no to child marriage.

articles.title: Two women booked over use of banned VPNs in Poonch; absconder held after two decades in Reasi: Officials
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: In 2025, the District Magistrate, Poonch, issued prohibitory orders on the use of VPN apps in the district close to the Line of Control (LoC) and also considered as an infiltration route of terrorists
Two women were booked on Thursday in the Pir Panjal valley’s Poonch district over the use of Virtual Private Network (VPN) apps in violation of prohibitory orders of the District Magistrate.

Officials identified the two women as Muneera Bi and Soniya Ayoub, both residents of Poonch’s Ari. Two separate First Information Reports (FIRs) were lodged under Section 223 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), which deals with disobedience to an order duly promulgated by a public servant.

In 2025, the District Magistrate, Poonch, issued prohibitory orders on the use of VPN apps in the district close to the Line of Control (LoC) and also considered as an infiltration route of terrorists.
Meanwhile, police officials warned to carry out action against those using VPN apps in the district and advised people to follow the official directions.

Meanwhile, the J&K Police in Reasi claimed to have arrested a long-evading absconder, who was a surrendered terrorist, after two decades in connection with multiple terror cases, including the killing of a police personnel.

The police identified the accused as Mohammad Mansha, a resident of Thuroo Lassoli, Reasi. The accused was facing charges under Sections 302, 307 and 121-A of the Ranbir Penal Code and Sections 7/25 of the Arms Act in a case of killing of a policeman.

However, the accused was declared an absconder after the Reasi court issued an arrest warrant in 2001. “A District Absconder Tracking Unit was constituted and deputed to Tral, Awantipora (in Kashmir). Through professional expertise, perseverance and effective inter-district coordination, the team successfully traced and apprehended the accused,” said officials.

The police said the accused was allegedly an active terrorist during 2000-2007, before surrendering in 2007. The police said the arrest marks a significant achievement in bringing a long-pending pursuit to a successful conclusion after more than two decades.

articles.title: Strobe Talbott, former Time magazine reporter and Deputy Secretary of State, has died
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: While at the British university, after interning for Time in Moscow, the magazine asked Talbott to help translate the leaked memoirs of Nikita Khrushchev

Strobe Talbott, a former Time magazine reporter who later served as Deputy Secretary of State under President Bill Clinton and then headed the Brookings Institution, died Thursday (November 26, 2026). He was 80.
His son, Devin Talbott, confirmed he passed away peacefully after a long illness in his East Hampton, New York, home.

The elder Talbott was educated at Yale and Oxford, where he bunked with Mr. Clinton. While at the British university, after interning for Time in Moscow, the magazine asked Talbott to help translate the leaked memoirs of Nikita Khrushchev, the former first secretary of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union, who was ousted in 1964.
Talbott did, and it gave him some notoriety as a young man and a job at the magazine.

After 21 years at Time , where he focused on Soviet-American relations and held positions including Washington bureau chief and a foreign-affairs columnist, according to his US State Department biography, he received a call from the newly elected Clinton.
Then-Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao in conversation with visiting then-U.S. Deputy Secretary of State Strobe Talbot, in New Delhi on April 08, 1994. | Photo Credit: UNI

Talbott joined the U.S. State Department in 1994, swiftly becoming Deputy Secretary of State. In that role, he was the architect of the Clinton administration's approach to Russia and other formerly Soviet countries and conducted negotiations between the US and India after the latter's nuclear tests in 1998.
Afterward, he served as the president of Brookings from 2002 to 2017. In that time, he also chaired the U.S. State Department's Foreign Affairs Policy Board.
Talbott also authored over a dozen books. His last book was titled “Our Founders' Warning: The Age of Reason Meets the Age of Trump,” which was published in 2020.

He was born in Dayton, Ohio, in 1946, and is survived by two sons, Devin and Adrian; stepdaughter Rebecca Ascher-Walsh; siblings Kirk, Marjo and Page Talbott; and eight grandchildren, according to the New York Times.
His first wife, Brook Shearer, died in 2009, and he later married author Barbara Lazear Ascher.

Then-Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao in conversation with visiting then-U.S. Deputy Secretary of State Strobe Talbot, in New Delhi on April 08, 1994. | Photo Credit: UNI

Talbott joined the U.S. State Department in 1994, swiftly becoming Deputy Secretary of State. In that role, he was the architect of the Clinton administration's approach to Russia and other formerly Soviet countries and conducted negotiations between the US and India after the latter's nuclear tests in 1998.

Afterward, he served as the president of Brookings from 2002 to 2017. In that time, he also chaired the U.S. State Department's Foreign Affairs Policy Board.

Talbott also authored over a dozen books. His last book was titled “Our Founders' Warning: The Age of Reason Meets the Age of Trump,” which was published in 2020.

He was born in Dayton, Ohio, in 1946, and is survived by two sons, Devin and Adrian; stepdaughter Rebecca Ascher-Walsh; siblings Kirk, Marjo and Page Talbott; and eight grandchildren, according to the New York Times.

His first wife, Brook Shearer, died in 2009, and he later married author Barbara Lazear Ascher.

articles.title: Constitution is the guiding force for present, future, says Haryana CM Saini; Congress accuses BJP of undermining democracy
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Respecting the Constitution is not the responsibility of any one political party or government, but the duty of every individual whom the people have entrusted with the opportunity to serve them, said Nayab Singh Saini

Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini on Thursday (November 26, 2026) said that the Constitution is the guiding force for our present and future, which has shown the country the right path in overcoming every challenge, even as the Congress party accused the BJP of undermining democratic conventions, the independence of constitutional institutions and the voting rights of citizens.

“Over the past 77 years, the Constitution has shown the country the right path in overcoming every challenge. Respecting the Constitution is not the responsibility of any one political party or government, but the duty of every individual whom the people have entrusted with the opportunity to serve them,” said Mr. Saini, addressing the House during the special session of the Haryana State Assembly on the 77th anniversary of the adoption of the Constitution.

He said that the true tribute to the framers of the Constitution would be to uphold the democratic path shown by them, maintain its decorum and contribute to building an India where justice is accessible to all, opportunities are available to everyone and the dignity of every citizen is protected.

Meanwhile, as part of the party’s nationwide demonstration, Haryana Congress organised a ‘Samvidhan Raksha March’ in Panchkula. Led by AICC In-charge for Haryana Sanjay Dutt, Haryana Pradesh Congress Committee President Rao Narender Singh, and Congress Legislature Party Leader and former Chief Minister Bhupinder Singh Hooda, the march drew senior party leaders.

Addressing the gathering, Mr. Dutt said that the country is passing through a decisive phase in which protecting the Constitution and democracy is no longer merely a political issue, but a question concerning the future of the nation. “Intoxicated by its arrogance of power, the BJP government is undermining democratic conventions, the independence of constitutional institutions and the voting rights of citizens. Elections are the greatest expression of democracy. However, when serious questions are raised about the integrity of electoral rolls, complaints emerge regarding the deletion of voters’ names and doubts arise over the transparency of the electoral process, it signals a grave threat to the entire democratic framework.”

Mr. Hooda said that any attack on the Constitution is a direct attack on the country’s democratic framework and the rights of its citizens. “The Congress Party will continue its struggle, both on the streets and inside legislatures, to safeguard the Constitution, the independence of constitutional institutions and free and fair elections,” he said.
The HPCC president said “The anti-people policies and the BJP Government’s attitude towards democratic institutions have generated widespread public resentment.”

articles.title: Leave aside any differences, remove BJP in U.P., says Congress chief
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: ‘To win, we all have to fight together and leave aside egoistic talk; we have to strengthen the alliance and remove Modi-Yogi from power,’ said Mallikarjun Kharge

Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on Thursday (November 26, 2026) in Lucknow urged party leaders and workers to strengthen the Samajwadi Party (SP)-Congress alliance and leave aside any differences in a bid to oust the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in Uttar Pradesh. “To win, we all have to fight together and leave aside egoistic talk. We have to strengthen the alliance and remove Modi-Yogi from power. Narendra Modi and Gyanesh Kumar are forming an alliance and snatching the right to vote from the people through Special Intensive Revision (SIR) and EVM manipulation,” said Mr. Kharge, addressing a Constitution Day event at the State Congress office in Lucknow.

Highlighting the contribution of the grand old party in the freedom struggle and the deepening of India’s democracy, Mr. Kharge added, “Congress is a party that works together with everyone. It is the result of this collective effort that every citizen of the country has the right to vote today. We fought to save Baba Saheb’s Constitution and our rights through voting in 2024. This time too, if we work unitedly, we will definitely win”.

Hitting out at Union Home Minister Amit Shah over allegedly disrespecting Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, the Congress chief added, “Amit Shah said in Parliament, 'It has become fashionable to invoke Baba Saheb Ambedkar’s name. If you had invoked God’s name so much, you would have attained heaven.’ You people yourself are stealing in the name of Lord Ram; you are not going to get heaven”.

Later, in the day Congress State unit leaders were detained while taking out Constitution Protection March. “We [Congressmen] were taking out the ‘Constitution Protection March’ peacefully and were detained, but our resolve to protect the Constitution became stronger. The place may change; the paths may be blocked, but the struggle to protect the Constitution has not stopped and will not stop,” said Anil Yadav, a senior Congress leader. Lucknow police took Congress leaders to Lucknow’s Eco Garden and freed in the evening.

“The BJP government cannot tolerate even voices raised in support of the Constitution and democracy. The police force’s arrest of Congress leaders and workers who peacefully took to the streets, vowing to defend the Constitution, is deeply shameful. Is it now a crime to demand protection of our Constitution?

“Remember, the repression of power cannot erase the values ​​of the Constitution, nor can it silence the voice of democracy. Congress will continue its struggle until the rights of every citizen, the power of every vote, and the Constitution are respected,” said Dwijendra Tripathi, a senior Congress worker based in Lucknow.

articles.title: Delhi HC sets aside Centre’s order cancelling FCRA licence of NGO
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: ‘Based on the record, this court is unable to discern any material based on which it could be said that the appellant’s activities would likely prejudicially affect the sovereignty, integrity, or security of India or public interest,’ Justice A.J. Bhambhani said

The Delhi High Court on Thursday (November 26, 2026) set aside the Centre’s order cancelling the FCRA licence of NGO Socio Legal Information Centre (SLIC), holding that the allegation of the organisation engaging in “aggressive anti-government political activism” was unsupported by any material.
Editorial | Troubling bill: On the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026

“Based on the record, this court is unable to discern any material based on which it could be said that the appellant’s activities would likely prejudicially affect the sovereignty, integrity, or security of India or public interest,” Justice A.J. Bhambhani said.

The judge added, “The respondent’s allegation that the appellant has indulged in “aggressive anti-government political activism”, is also not based on any material. No documents or other material has been placed on record by the respondent to support that allegation”.
Editorial | ​Fear of the foreign: On the FCRA amendments

The court further opined that the October 17, 2022 cancellation order the organisation’s FCRA registration was “misconceived, untenable and illegal, apart from being disproportionate and excessive in its rigour and impact”.

The court passed the judgment on a plea by the NGO seeking to set aside the October 2022 order of the Ministry of Home Affairs cancelling its Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act registration certificate.
The NGO also challenged the freezing of its designated foreign contribution account and its utilisation accounts maintained with several banks across the country.
Editorial | Onerous rules: On the amended FCRA Rules, the fallout

The high court said the violations alleged in the cancellation order principally arise from the conditions for grant of an FCRA registration certificate, the essence of the allegation being that the NGO is guilty of diversion or misutilisation of such funds, or of using such funds for personal gains or diverting them for undesirable purposes.

“However, upon examining the use to which foreign contributions have been put by the appellant, it is seen that such funds have been utilised and deployed for activities that are perfectly in line with the stated objectives of the appellant, namely, of providing legal-aid and engaging in social welfare activities,” Justice Bhambhani said.

The court, in its 69-page judgment, said unless something sinister comes through from material available against it, an organisation that is engaged in assisting aggrieved persons in raising their grievances before courts and statutory commissions, acting through the available constitutional machinery, cannot be characterised as engaging in “political activity” or in activities impinging on political and law-and-order domains.

articles.title: Shocked to see use of heavy equipment at Sheshnag, no need for motorable roads to pilgrimages: Dr. Karan Singh
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: ‘I was shocked to read that heavy earth moving equipment is being used to widen the route to Shri Amarnath ji, and that too at a spot overlooking Sheshnag, which is one of the most beautiful lakes in India,’ said Dr. Karan Singh

Senior J&K politician Karan Singh on Thursday expressed shock over the use of heavy earth-moving equipment to widen the route to the Amarnath shrine close to the Sheshnag lake in Kashmir. Meanwhile, Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) president Mehbooba Mufti asked J&K Chief Minister Omar Abdullah to withdraw the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Border Roads Organisation (BRO) and explain the use of heavy machinery at the high-altitude glacial lake.

“I was shocked to read that heavy earth-moving equipment is being used to widen the route to Shri Amarnath ji, and that too at a spot overlooking Sheshnag, which is one of the most beautiful lakes in India. I join my voice with those who are protesting about this, and would urge those concerned not to use heavy equipment on this route,” said Mr. Singh, who also served as the last Dogra Maharaja of J&K.

He cautioned that there was no need “to make every pilgrim route into a motorable road just for the convenience of tourists”. “Genuine pilgrims will not mind walking or riding towards this great shrine. For many years I have been raising the disaster being caused to the Himalayas due to avoidable road widening, particularly on the pilgrim routes in Uttarakhand. I see no reason why tourists and pilgrims cannot manage with two-lane roads,” said Mr. Singh.

He said in the name of tourists an unnecessary programme of road widening is underway, which involves extensive use of dynamite which severely damages the comparatively young Himalayas. “In fact, several disasters have already occurred, including the one at Kedarnath some years ago,” said Mr. Singh, in a statement.
In a post on X, Mr. Singh’s son Vikramaditya Singh termed it “a collective duty to preserve the natural beauty and unique ecology of J&K for future generations”.

“The felling and burning of protected Chinar and Chestnut trees in Kashmir, along with BRO road construction in close proximity to the sacred Sheshnag Lake, are deeply concerning developments. The fragile ecosystem of J&K, already under considerable stress, cannot afford such irreversible damage. I urge the J&K Government and the concerned authorities to take serious cognisance of these activities and ensure strict monitoring before it is too late,” said Mr. Singh.
Meanwhile, Ms. Mufti of the PDP expressed dissatisfaction over J&K Forest minister Altaf Kalooo’s statement that “all was well at the Sheshnag lake and there was no violation at the site”.
Addressing a press conference in Srinagar, Ms. Mufti demanded that the Omar Abdullah government should halt use of heavy machines like JCB and cancel the MoU with the BRO.

“The JCB should be removed from Sheshnag and the work stopped till environment specialists visit the site. Also. the MoU signed with the BRO should be made public. The MoU signed by the government should be brought to the public domain. Is the use of JCB part of the MoU?” said Ms. Mufti.

articles.title: Thirupparankundram 'deepathoon' row LIVE: Supreme Court to pass interim orders over failure to light Karthigai Deepam lamp
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Contempt petitioners allege at the apex court that the State had already decided to not comply with the order

The Collector had tendered a formal apology, attempted to shift the blame entirely to the devasthanam . Surprised that a collector is taking this stance, his powers are wide enought to implement the orders of this court.
We are not satisfied with his preliminary report. Have to see whether his account reflects what happened. The stand of the Collector reminds of “pretending to cry”.
We are prima facie satisfied the November 20 order wilfully disobeyed.
Supreme Court delivers the judgement on the contempt proceedings
The Supreme Court holds that the actions, omissions of the Executive authorities prima facie reveal wilful disobedience of the court order of November 20.
The chain of events indicate that the Executive authorities have acted according to the dictates of their political bosses.
The Chief Secretary of Tamil Nadu is to file an affidavit with calls, emails, communications and he shall appear before this court.

The Supreme Court said: Apt and appropriate to say the board has never appeared or contested the matter by impugning the order. When this court speaks, it speaks with the authority of the Constitution. It has to be obeyed. The Executive authorities has wilfully disobeyed. Strikes at the very root of law. Have to be dealt with iron hands.

The Supreme Court said: The trustees have categorically taken a stand they would not comply with the Supreme Court order. Serious infraction on thir part aided by State authorities. Wilful and flagarant disobedience of the court order. It reveals an undermining of authority of the court. Shocks the court’s conscience. This court had examined both parties, traditions of the court. Unnecessary insinuations being brought against court.
The Thirupparankundram lamplighting litigation has a chequered history, the Supreme Court notes in the order.

“In the light of prohibitory orders issued by the DM under S.163 BNSS, certain devotees had moved the Madras HC. The District Administration led by Collector had given an undertaking to comply with the Supreme Court November 20 order. Despite this, the authorities allegedly colluded with temple adminsitration to light the lamp at the Uchipillaiyar temple.

“Brazen and mutual disobedience of this court’s order. Calculated affront to the authority of the Supreme Court. Devasthanam board purportedly overreached the order of the court by giving a strained interpretation of the November 20 order. The Collector is taking umbrage under a resolution of the devasthanam,” the apex court said.

articles.title: Suspected JeM operative held in Vadodara; planned to attack IAF station, says ATS
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The ATS team recovered an assault rifle, suspected to be an AK-47, 23 live cartridges, two empty cartridges, a JeM flag, mobile phones and SIM cards from his possession, says ATS DIG Sunil Josh

The Gujarat Anti-Terrorist Squad (ATS) has arrested a suspected Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM) operative with an assault weapon and ammunition in Vadodara, foiling an alleged plot to attack the Indian Air Force (IAF) station in the city, officials said on Friday (November 27, 2026).

The accused, Mohommad Saharul Islam Kabiruddin, a resident of Karimganj in Assam, was apprehended near a hotel on Halol-Vadodara Road on Thursday (November 26) night based on technical and human intelligence inputs, ATS Deputy Inspector General (DIG) Sunil Joshi said.
The ATS team recovered an assault rifle, suspected to be an AK-47, 23 live cartridges, two empty cartridges, a JeM flag, mobile phones and SIM cards from his possession, he said.

During interrogation, it came to light that the accused was allegedly tasked with attacking the gate of the IAF station in Vadodara, and photographs of the establishment were recovered from his mobile phone, the official said.
A case has been registered against him under relevant provisions of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) and the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), officials added.

articles.title: IORA nations must enhance collaboration: EAM Jaishankar
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar says the 23-member grouping must strengthen its collective voice amid geopolitical changes, as India chairs the Indian Ocean Rim Association

The Indian Ocean is central to global trade, energy security and connectivity, and all littoral states in the region must jointly work towards “meaningful collaboration” in ensuring a better future for its people, External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar said on Friday (November 27, 2026).

In an address at a ministerial conclave of the Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA), Mr. Jaishankar said the grouping must reinforce its role as a regional platform at a time of significant “geopolitical changes”.

India hosted the conclave in New Delhi in its capacity as the current chair of the IORA, which comprises 23 nations, including Australia, Indonesia, South Africa, Kenya, Tanzania, Mozambique, Somalia, Oman, Yemen, Bangladesh, Malaysia and Thailand.

“The Indian Ocean is central to global trade, energy security, connectivity and economic prosperity. It is also a region of immense diversity, opportunity and shared challenges,” Mr. Jaishankar said in his opening remarks at the meeting.
He said India’s approach to the IORA and its chairship of the bloc is guided by the MAHASAGAR vision.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced the MAHASAGAR vision, or “Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions”, for India’s engagement with the Global South during his visit to Mauritius in March 2025.

Mr. Jaishankar said India’s theme for the IORA — Innovation, Openness, Resilience and Adaptability in the Indian Ocean Region — reflects its conviction that the grouping must remain responsive and adaptive to various challenges.
“At a time of significant geopolitical changes, IORA must enhance its collective voice and reinforce its role as a regional platform,” he said.
“Achieving these requires greater coordination among member states, meaningful collaboration with dialogue partners and a stronger focus on practical cooperation,” he said.

articles.title: APSRTC to pay drivers cleared in accident inquiries, assign alternative duties during licence suspension
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The decision follows a representation from the employees’ Joint Action Committee, which says suspended licences leave drivers without work or pay

The Andhra Pradesh State Road Transport Corporation (APSRTC) has decided to assign alternative duties and pay salaries to the drivers involved in road accidents if departmental inquiries establish that they are not at fault, even if their driving licences have been suspended by the Regional Transport Authority (RTA).

APSRTC Joint Managing Director M. Siva Prasad has issued a notification directing Executive Directors, District Public Transport Officers (DPTOs), depot managers and unit officers to provide alternative (out-of-designation) duties to such drivers until their licences are restored.

The decision follows a representation from the employees’ Joint Action Committee (JAC), which said that drivers involved in fatal road accidents often face suspension of their driving licences under Section 19 of the Motor Vehicles Act. In cases where departmental inquiries establish that the drivers are not at fault, the suspension nevertheless leaves them unable to perform their regular duties and earn their salaries.
Taking note of the issue, the APSRTC management decided to provide temporary alternative assignments to drivers cleared in departmental inquiries until their driving licences are reinstated.
Under the new guidelines, depot managers and unit officers concerned should write to the respective RTAs seeking restoration of the licences of eligible drivers.

Meanwhile, the drivers should be temporarily assigned duties other than their regular driving responsibilities. DPTOs may approve alternative assignments for drivers whose licences have been suspended for up to three months. In cases involving suspension for more than three months, approval should be obtained from Executive Directors or zonal authorities.
The notification also stipulates that drivers assigned alternative duties during the suspension period should be paid their salaries.

The JMD directed all depot managers, unit officers and other officials concerned to implement the instructions strictly with the objective of ensuring justice to drivers while utilising their services for the corporation’s operational needs.

fullParagraphs: Declines to comment on ongoing war of words and the appearance of flex boards supporting various party leaders in Keralam

In Kozhikode district, similar boards, claiming to have been put up by Youth Congress workers, appeared near the District Congress Committee (DCC) office, Christian College Junction and Vadakara.

articles.title: CPI(M) slams Keralam govt over ban on party newspapers in jails
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The CPI(M) on Friday strongly criticised the Congress-led government over the decision to stop the distribution of political party-affiliated newspapers in jails, questioning whether a “super Emergency” had been declared in Keralam.

Senior party leader M V Jayarajan told reporters in Kannur that a circular directing prisons to stop purchasing and distributing newspapers, including Deshabhimani , the CPI(M)’s mouthpiece, was issued by the Director General of Prisons a day ago.
“Has a super Emergency been declared in Keralam? Chief Minister V D Satheesan and Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala should clarify this,” he said.

Mr. Jayarajan pointed out that even during the Emergency, newspapers, including Deshabhimani , were allowed in State prisons. At that time, certain news reports were blacked out due to press censorship to prevent inmates from accessing them, he said.
There was no such situation now, and the present ban was a “primitive” move, he alleged.
He also said prison rules stipulated that newspapers sent to inmates by their friends or relatives through sponsorships should be provided to them.
The present restriction was against these rules, Jayarajan said, alleging that the Director General of Prisons would not have issued such a circular without the knowledge of the home minister.

His criticism came a day after the Kerala Prisons and Correctional Services Department directed all jails in the state to stop purchasing and distributing newspapers and publications affiliated to political parties.

In a circular issued on Thursday, Director General of Prisons S Sreejith said correctional institutions, which aim at the psychological and social rehabilitation of inmates, should ensure that the news and information made available to them were objective, truthful and free from political bias.
Publications serving as mouthpieces of political parties or organisations, or reflecting political interests, were not appropriate for distribution in prisons, the circular said.

articles.title: Pakistan set to host talks with Saudi Arabia, Turkey under trilateral defence pact
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The talks in Islamabad will focus on West Asia and the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, two security officials said, with Pakistan’s Defence and Foreign Ministers and army chief attending

Pakistan is set to host talks with Saudi Arabia and Turkiye on Friday (November 27, 2026) under a trilateral defence pact that treats an attack on any member as an attack on all three, two security officials said.

The talks in Islamabad will focus on developments in West Asia, including ongoing attacks on Saudi Arabia by Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi rebels, the officials said. They spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorised to discuss the meeting publicly.

Pakistan has said that the agreement is purely defensive in nature and not against anyone, including Iran, and that the trilateral alliance reflects a shared desire to strengthen strategic security cooperation.

Senior diplomats as well as defence and military officials from the three countries are expected to discuss ways to deter threats, expand military cooperation, share intelligence and strengthen defence industry ties, the officials said. Pakistan’s Defence Minister Khawaja Muhammad Asif, Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar and army chief Field Marshal Asim Munir will attend the meeting.
Mr. Asif has said that Pakistan will use “whatever means are available” to defend Saudi Arabia against attacks from the Houthis.

However, Pakistan is still making efforts, with help from countries in West Asia, including Qatar, to urge the United States and Iran to return to the negotiating table to end the conflict in the region and beyond through talks. Pakistan had brokered an interim deal between the two sides in June 2026.

Friday’s meeting of the Strategic, Political and Defense Committee falls under the Joint Mecca Defense Agreement, which was signed in August 2026 in the Saudi holy city of Mecca by Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Pakistan’s Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif.

Pakistan’s government has not released details ahead of the meeting, but the authorities have declared a local holiday in Islamabad to limit public movement as part of security measures for the gathering. Islamabad traffic police have announced road diversions and advised motorists to use alternative routes to accommodate the movement of foreign delegations.

During a previous meeting in Riyadh, the three sides had vowed to immediately implement what they said were their collective defence commitments, including arrangements for the rapid deployment of agreed-upon military forces and capabilities to Saudi Arabia.

According to the agreement, the group’s secretariat has been established in Saudi Arabia, and retired Pakistani General Nauman Mahmood has been selected as its first secretary-general. He will also attend Friday’s meeting. The pact binds the parties for 10 years, after which they would need to give three months’ notice before leaving.

articles.title: Costa Rica bars entry to UN rapporteur over ‘links to terrorist acts’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Francesca Albanese arrived at the airport serving the capital, San Jose, to receive an honorary degree from the University of Costa Rica, a public university

Costa Rica's government said on Thursday (November 26, 2026) it had denied entry to UN rapporteur Francesca Albanese, who has accused Israel of genocide, because she was the subject of an "international alert over links to terrorist acts."

Ms. Albanese, the UN special rapporteur on the Palestinian territories, arrived on Thursday (November 26) at the airport serving the capital, San Jose, to receive an honorary degree from the University of Costa Rica, a public university.

Ms. Albanese "is the subject of an international alert over links to terrorist acts," Omer Badilla, director general of Costa Rica's immigration authority, which falls under the interior ministry, said in a video posted on social media.
"I hope this clears up any doubts and makes clear the threat this woman poses to national security," he added.

The rector's office at the institution, the country's most important and prestigious university, said in a statement that immigration authorities were "blocking" Ms. Albanese's entry and asked the government to explain the decision.
The government of Costa Rican President Laura Fernández is a close ally of U.S. President Donald Trump and has pursued closer trade ties with Israel since she took office in May.

Last December, Ms. Albanese criticised a free trade agreement between Costa Rica and Israel and called for its ratification to be put on hold, prompting a rebuke from the government, which accused her of interfering in domestic affairs.
The United States, Israel's main ally, imposed sanctions on Ms. Albanese after she criticised Washington's policy on Gaza.
"You see the face of empire the day you touch a nerve or cross its boundaries," Ms. Albanese wrote from the airport.

The university said it was awarding the honorary doctorate, which it grants annually to a prominent figure, in recognition of her "solid academic background, experience, publications and work exposing wrongdoing."

The Italian independent expert has faced harsh criticism from Israel and some of its allies over her longstanding accusations that Israel has committed genocide and other war crimes against Palestinians in Gaza and the occupied West Bank.
Israel's ambassador to the United Nations, Danny Danon, welcomed Costa Rica's decision.

articles.title: Canada’s top court rules on Quebec secularism law in landmark case
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The law has been the subject of intense legal debate since it was first passed by Quebec's government in 2019
The Supreme Court rules on Friday (November 27, 2026) on one of Canada's most closely watched cases -- a Quebec law barring some provincial employees from wearing religious symbols.
The law has been the subject of intense legal debate since it was first passed by Quebec's government in 2019.

That is partly due to the implications for Quebec, a majority French-speaking province where the decades-long battle to enforce secularism is a core issue and where the Catholic Church once wielded enormous influence over public life.

The case reflects a conflict playing out elsewhere in the world as strictly secular states such as that of France face pressure typical of the Anglo-Saxon world for people to be able to practice their religion freely, including wearing whatever symbols of it that they wish.
The Quebec case is also seen as a major test of how far provinces can go in defying provisions of the federal constitution by invoking the so-called "notwithstanding clause."
That clause, a quirk of Canada's legal system, effectively allows provincial governments to pass laws that may breach Canada's constitution, known as the Charter of Rights and Freedoms.

Quebec pre-emptively invoked the "notwithstanding clause" when passing its secularism bill, anticipating it would be challenged over constitutional protections guaranteeing freedom of religion and expression.
Conservative-led provinces have also invoked the clause to defend legislation relating to transgender youth.
In 2023, Saskatchewan used the clause to pass a law requiring schools to obtain parental consent before changing the pronouns used for children under 16.

🌐 International Affairs 📅 27 Nov 2026 • IN-APP NEWSPAPER PRINT EDITION

Canada’s top court rules on Quebec secularism law in landmark case

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics

The law has been the subject of intense legal debate since it was first passed by Quebec's government in 2019

The Supreme Court rules on Friday (November 27, 2026) on one of Canada's most closely watched cases -- a Quebec law barring some provincial employees from wearing religious symbols.

The law has been the subject of intense legal debate since it was first passed by Quebec's government in 2019.

That is partly due to the implications for Quebec, a majority French-speaking province where the decades-long battle to enforce secularism is a core issue and where the Catholic Church once wielded enormous influence over public life.

The case reflects a conflict playing out elsewhere in the world as strictly secular states such as that of France face pressure typical of the Anglo-Saxon world for people to be able to practice their religion freely, including wearing whatever symbols of it that they wish.

The Quebec case is also seen as a major test of how far provinces can go in defying provisions of the federal constitution by invoking the so-called "notwithstanding clause."

That clause, a quirk of Canada's legal system, effectively allows provincial governments to pass laws that may breach Canada's constitution, known as the Charter of Rights and Freedoms.

Quebec pre-emptively invoked the "notwithstanding clause" when passing its secularism bill, anticipating it would be challenged over constitutional protections guaranteeing freedom of religion and expression.

Conservative-led provinces have also invoked the clause to defend legislation relating to transgender youth.

In 2023, Saskatchewan used the clause to pass a law requiring schools to obtain parental consent before changing the pronouns used for children under 16.

Alberta has also invoked the clause in relation to laws banning transgender girls from participating in female sports and restricting hormone therapy for individuals under 16.

The Supreme Court's ruling in the Quebec case will be scrutinized for potential national impact.

It says public employees in certain positions of authority, such as judges, police officers and teachers, cannot wear religious symbols.

articles.title: AirAsia delays staff salary payments to end of month, internal email shows
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Salary payments during the five-month period would be made on the 30th of each month ‌or the last day of February, the notice said

AirAsia has ‌told employees it will delay salary payments to the end of each month ​from November through March, according to an internal email seen by Reuters , as ⁠the airline takes measures to conserve cash and its Philippine unit cuts jobs.

The email, sent to Malaysia-based staff late last week by Chief People Officer Muhammad Khurram Zia, cited the need for a “temporary operational adjustment” at ‌Southeast Asia’s largest budget airline, which like its peers faces higher jet fuel costs.
Salary payments during the five-month period would be made on the 30th of each month ‌or the last day of February, the email said.
It cited a “challenging environment” and asked employees ‌for “patience ⁠and flexibility.”
The email’s contents were confirmed by two people familiar with the matter. ⁠One of the people said AirAsia had previously paid salaries earlier in the second half of each month.
The Iran war has sent jet fuel prices soaring, putting airlines worldwide under their ​worst financial strain since the COVID-19 pandemic.

U.S. low-cost ‌carrier Spirit Airlines collapsed in May, Latvia’s airBaltic sought bankruptcy protection in September and Norway’s Norse Atlantic suspended flights on Thursday as it looks for urgent short-term financing.
Shares in AirAsia, which employs about 26,000 people predominantly in Asia, have declined more than 70% ‌this year as elevated fuel prices and foreign exchange losses squeezed its operations.
AirAsia Philippines said ​on Thursday (November 26, 2026) it would reduce its workforce following sustained pressure on its operating costs, without specifying how many staff would be affected.

The airline said on Friday (November 27) it ⁠remained fully operational and committed to serving the Philippine market. The planned workforce adjustment will not affect passenger flights, bookings, or other services, AirAsia Philippines General Manager and President Anna Victoria Lu said in a ‌statement.
The AirAsia Philippines Pilots’ Union filed notice of a strike after 90 pilots were retrenched, its president said in a video posted on social media on Thursday (November 26).
Philippine Labor Secretary Francis Tolentino confirmed receiving notice in a text message to Reuters.

articles.title: 200-year-old Taj Mahal marble slab to be auctioned in U.K.
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The rectangular slab is estimated to fetch between 20,000 and 30,000 pounds (₹24-36 lakh approximately)
An intricate floral-bordered marble slab taken from the Taj Mahal in Agra by an officer of the East India Company is set to be auctioned in the U.K. next month.

The rectangular slab, one of two that Colonel Pownoll Phipps collected in 1816 at the end of his tenure as superintendent of the repairs of the buildings in and around Agra, is estimated to fetch between 20,000 and 30,000 pounds (₹24-36 lakh approximately).
It is being offered as part of the Islamic and Indian Art sale by Lyon and Turnbull auctioneers on December 9.

“The marble slab is accompanied by a vintage black and white photograph of the Taj Mahal and two letters — one printed by the grandson of Colonel Pownoll and one handwritten by the Marquess of Bath,” the auction notes state.

The colonel’s son's memoirs quote that his father found them in a ‘souterrain’, or underground area, at the Taj Mahal and that he thought they were intended for the repairs to the iconic Mughal-era monument.
Colonel Pownoll Phipps was born in Devon, England, in 1780. Hailing from a line of soldiers since the early 17th century, he joined the East India Company as a cadet in the Bengal Army in 1799.

After battling troops in Egypt, Phipps returned to India, where he quickly rose through the ranks, becoming Fort-Adjutant and Barrack-Master at Agra in 1809, where he remained for the next seven years.
During the colonial era, he was responsible among other things for the care of the Taj Mahal and other historic buildings.

“He took this job most seriously and was at times called upon to prevent damage by Europeans looking for keepsakes. As his son wrote, ‘he was once sent for to the Taj, where, in spite of the remonstrances of the sentry, an English lady was insisting on picking agates out of the marble with a steel fork’,” the auctioneers note.
In 1816, the colonel was chosen by the Governor General of India to become Superintendent of Building in the Lower Provinces, which meant leaving Agra for Kolkata.
His interest in the art and architecture of India remained, however, and he maintained “a staff of very skilful native draughtsmen” who made detailed images of the buildings under his care.
He and his family returned to Britain in 1823, and he died there in 1858. The slab was in the family’s collection for over 200 years.

articles.title: Donald Trump urges Vladimir Putin to end ‘military aggression’ in Europe
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Donald Trump said he had requested Vladimir Putin when they met in China last week, adding that he thought it would help lead to a deal to end Moscow's grinding war in Ukraine

U.S. President Donald Trump said on Thursday (November 26, 2026) he had asked Vladimir Putin to "pull back all military aggression" against Europe, in a fresh shift in tone towards the Russian leader he called his friend just last week.
Mr. Trump said he had requested Mr. Putin when they met in China last week, adding that he thought it would help lead to a deal to end Moscow's grinding war in Ukraine.

"During my conversations in China with President Vladimir Putin, of Russia, I spent a lot of time talking about the fact that I would like to see President Putin pull back all Military aggression against territories throughout Europe," Mr. Trump said on his Truth Social network.
Mr. Trump said he had done so "in the hopes that a Deal can be made between Russia and Ukraine, and made quickly."
"I really believe this is a strong possibility," he added.

The statement did not specify which territories Mr. Trump meant -- and did not specifically include Ukraine, which Russia invaded in February 2022, kicking off the largest war in Europe since World War II.
European nations have been increasingly concerned by what they regard as Russian provocations, including three Russian cruise missiles landing in NATO-member Poland last week.

In their joint statement on Wednesday (November 25), Mr. Trump and Mr. Rutte said they "discussed the importance of Russia avoiding any actions that intentionally, or unintentionally, expand the war."
In a notable contrast with Mr. Trump's recent criticisms of Ukraine for striking targets deep inside Russia, the U.S. leader made no call for Kyiv to show similar restraint.

Speaking to reporters at his Mar-a-Lago estate in Florida on Thursday (November 26), Mr. Trump said he was unsure if Mr. Putin would be coming to the G20 summit next month in Miami, but "but if he wanted to come, he certainly can."
Mr. Trump's tone appeared markedly different to when Mr. Trump met Mr. Putin in the Chinese city of Shenzhen last week, both face-to-face and together with Chinese President Xi Jinping.
Mr. Trump warmly greeted Mr. Putin and called him his "friend" at the summit, renewing concerns in Kyiv and European capitals that he was once again pivoting towards the Russian leader.

articles.title: Elevated blood sugar during adulthood linked with worse cognition in midlife: study
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The findings suggest that changes in glucose metabolism may affect brain health earlier in adulthood than previously thought

Young adults with progressively increasing fasting blood sugar may be more likely to have a poor cognitive functioning by midlife, according to a new study that tracked young adults for over three decades.
The findings suggest that changes in glucose metabolism may affect brain health earlier in adulthood than previously thought.
Participants who developed type 2 diabetes during the study also showed signs of structural brain changes, according to findings published in the Journal of the American Heart Association .

"Diabetes is known to affect cognitive function, but cognitive impairment due to diabetes was once believed to happen mostly during childhood among people with Type 1 diabetes or after age 65 in people with Type 2 diabetes," lead author Regina Paradela, a post-doctoral researcher at the University of São Paulo Medical School in São Paulo, Brazil, said.

"However, prediabetes and sustained elevated fasting blood sugar levels in adults without type 1 or type 2 diabetes may also have an increased risk of late-life cognitive decline and dementia," Paradela said.
The researchers suggested early monitoring and management of blood sugar levels in young adulthood -- 18 to 30 years old -- might be a strategy to preserve brain health.

Normal fasting blood glucose is generally below 100 milligrams per decilitre, 100-125 milligrams per decilitre indicates prediabetes and a value over 126 milligrams per decilitre is consistent with Type 2 diabetes.

"The fact that increasing glucose levels were associated with poorer cognitive performance, even among people who had not developed Type 2 diabetes during the 30-year study, is very important," Paradela said.
"This suggests that changes in glucose metabolism may be relevant to brain health earlier in adulthood than we typically think about," Paradela said.

The study is among the first to investigate and compare the association between changes in fasting blood sugar levels from early adulthood to changes in cognition and brain structure in middle age, over approximately 30 years, the researchers said.

Health data for nearly 3,000 participants in the Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults (CARDIA) study, which enrolled Black and white adults aged 18 to 30 in four US cities from 1985 to 1986, was analysed. MRI brain scans were taken for 605 participants.

Researchers identified three fasting blood sugar trajectories from young adulthood to midlife: lower-stable glucose (blood sugar), moderate-stable glucose and increasing glucose. About 345 participants developed diabetes during the 30-year follow-up.

fullParagraphs: In a time of global tension, digital overload and endless advice about raising children, experts say 2027 calls for a radical rethink: less perfection, more presence

Prem Kishore occasionally turns to Artificial Intelligence (AI) for help when it comes to raising his six-year-old son. “It’s the big feelings that can be difficult to talk about, because we don’t always have the right words. I usually seek advice from my friends or psychologists, but if they’re not available, I turn to AI,” says the creative professional, 43, who splits his time between Bengaluru and Dubai.
Kishore recalls how he visited an AI video generator to create an avatar of a doctor, who chatted with his son about healthy boundaries and consent.

As AI becomes more enmeshed in our day-to-day lives, families are turning to it for advice, research and assistance in managing the mental load of modern-day parenting. A 2026 consumer trends report by GIPSI, the research arm of agency Tonic Worldwide, combined search and social media data with a survey of 50,000 people, and found that 52% of Indian Gen Z parents now use AI instead of their usual search engines, and 48% use it as an adviser. In India, Google Gemini recently launched a series of commercials featuring Shah Rukh Khan in which he directs two fathers at very different stages of their parenting journeys towards the chatbot for advice. Apps such as Fambot and AVA seek to help families with administrative tasks by syncing to their calendars, email and online shopping orders.

Eighteen years ago, when I first became a parent, Dr. Spock’s Baby and Child Care was the de facto gift to all new parents along with a Johnson & Johnson baby care set. I kept the book for a number of years after I had my second child and referred to it frequently. But today, new parents can seek advice from podcasts, influencers, online communities and yes, AI chatbots. There is a lot of advice out there, available in seconds. But how much of it is actually helping parents?

Author-editor Sanjana Kapur, 40, who’s raising a nine-year-old in Bengaluru, admits that parenting feels a little nerve-racking today. “There’s so much information out there, that you’re constantly worrying if you’re making the right decision, or how even your smallest reaction will affect your child. The world has become such a complicated place, and parents are nervous even when kids are at school now,” she admits.

articles.title: WhatsApp to let users buy travel eSIMs in app; Jio, Verizon among partners
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: WhatsApp Head Kunal Shah described the effort as the company's early explorations around eSIMs in a post on X

WhatsApp will soon let users buy and install a data eSIM for international travel without leaving the app, so they can keep using it on their existing phone number abroad, the Meta-owned company said in a blog post on Thursday (November 26, 2026), naming Jio among its partners.

The company said it was working with eSIM providers and telecom partners, including Jio, Smart Axiata, Smart Communications and Verizon, and would begin rolling out the feature in select countries soon. It did not name the countries or give pricing details.

"...We’re announcing a new way to buy and install a data e-SIM when travelling internationally in just a few taps without leaving the app. It’ll be as effortless as sending a message. That way, when you land, you can keep using WhatsApp on your same phone number as you normally would without having to find the closest airport kiosk to buy a local SIM card, hunt for a cafe with Wi-Fi or rack up roaming charges,” WhatsApp said.
WhatsApp Head Kunal Shah described the effort as the company's early explorations around eSIMs in a post on X.

"What if WhatsApp could work anywhere you go in the world without any struggle," Shah wrote, adding, "Inviting partners everywhere to join us in this important mission." WhatsApp has more than 3 billion users worldwide, according to Meta.

articles.title: Sugar restriction during first 1000 days of life reduces cancer incidence, pace of ageing: study
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Researchers uncovered two pathways for this: people unexposed to sugar early ate smaller quantities, and maintained healthier, more diverse diets five decades later; they also exhibited a longer leukocyte telomere, the protective DNA–protein cap at the ends of chromosomes inside a white blood cell length

Reducing sugar exposure during the first 1,000 days of life is associated with a substantially lower cancer risk decades later, and a slower biological ageing process, the results of a U.K.-based study have shown.

The article , ‘ Early-life sugar restriction causally reduces adult cancer incidence and slows biological aging’ published in PNAS, analysed 64,761 adults in the U.K. Biobank, coinciding with a policy-level sugar rationing period in the U.K. People whose first 1,000 days occurred during sugar rationing had 36% to 69% lower incidence of liver/intrahepatic bile duct, rectal, prostate, breast, and lung cancers later in life. There were markers that indicated that these people had 2.2 fewer years of biological aging, and they were left with persistent healthier eating habits, even 50 years later.

articles.title: Motorola pivots to premiumisation, aims for third spot in India
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: According to the latest IDC report, Motorola has already climbed to become the fifth-largest smartphone brand in India, capturing an 8.8% market share during the third quarter of this year

Motorola is aiming for the third spot in India’s competitive smartphone market as the Lenovo-owned brand aggressively pivots to premiumisation and seamless connected experiences. The company’s executives outlined their strategic vision during a media visit at their contract partner Dixon (Padget Electronics) facility in Noida, Uttar Pradesh.

India’s smartphone market is currently being dominated by Samsung followed by two Chinese players (Vivo and Oppo). If Motorola continues its aggressive push and mix of products, it would be able to replace Oppo to become the third largest smartphone brand in the country.
According to the latest IDC report, Motorola has already climbed to become the fifth-largest smartphone brand in India, capturing an 8.8% market share during the third quarter of this year.

This growth is heavily anchored in its premium portfolio, which includes the Edge, Razr, and Signature series. Motorola reports that its revenue has surged 20-fold since FY19-20, with nearly 60% now driven entirely by these high-end devices.
Fueling this momentum is robust local manufacturing. Motorola’s upcoming premium flagship smartphone, the Motorola Signature 27, will be made at the Noida facility.

Alongside Dixon, the brand maintains a strategic manufacturing partnership with Neolync in Tirupati, Andhra Pradesh. Together, these facilities not only fulfill domestic demand but also handle exports to Latin and North American markets.

Motorola’s manufacturing expansion has generated a substantial economic footprint, providing direct employment to nearly 8,000 people and creating over 56,000 indirect opportunities spanning manufacturing, sales, and servicing.

To support its expanding market presence, Motorola has established an extensive service network across the country. The brand currently covers 716 PIN codes across 620 cities in India, supported by over 846 touch points and 685 dedicated repair centres.

Looking ahead, Motorola is doubling down on artificial intelligence, prioritising practical, day-to-day use cases. The company has partnered with Google to integrate Gemini Intelligence into its upcoming Signature 27.
Motorola continues to evolve its proprietary AI assistant, Qira, which is designed to enhance cross-device connectivity and deliver advanced productivity tools for users.

articles.title: Mirwaiz says he was put under house arrest over Vande Mataram issue, decries action against Maulana Qasimi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: It has become a precedent that every time I raise people’s issues and concerns, I am not allowed to go to Jama Masjid on that Friday, says the chief cleric

Kashmir chief cleric Mirwaiz Umar Farooq on Friday (November 27, 2026) said he was placed under house arrest and another prominent cleric, Maulana Rehmatullah Qasimi, was summoned to a police station over their opposition to the playing of Vande Mataram at a J&K Waqf Board function in Srinagar.

“I had anticipated that I would be punished this Friday by being put under house arrest. I also raised concerns over the recitation of Vande Mataram at the religious function of the J&K Waqf Board, as well as people’s grave concerns over the disaster-in-waiting in the ecologically fragile region of Sheshnag after the viral visuals,” the Mirwaiz said in a statement.
The Mirwaiz alleged he was “prevented from proceeding to Jama Masjid, Srinagar, to deliver the Friday sermon and offer congregational prayers.”
“It has become a precedent that every time I raise people’s issues and concerns, I am not allowed to go to Jama Masjid on that Friday,” the Mirwaiz said.
The chief cleric also expressed “deep regret” over the summoning of Mr. Qasimi, head of Kashmir’s largest seminary, Darul Uloom Raheemiyyah, in Bandipora.
Mr. Qasimi also spoke about the playing of Vande Mataram during the J&K Waqf Board Day on November 23 in Srinagar, which was attended by local imams and religious scholars.

“Yesterday (Thursday), Kashmir’s renowned Islamic scholar and patron of the Mutahida Majlis-e-Ulama, Maulana Rehmatullah Qasimi Sahib, was summoned to the police station and reprimanded. Can we no longer raise our voices to safeguard our religious beliefs and sentiments? Do we not even have the right to express our religious concerns?” the Mirwaiz said.

articles.title: Why Delimitation Bill failed to pass in Parliament in April 2026
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Why the Delimitation Bill failed in Parliament in April 2026 and how the political arithmetic changed since then; here’s what to know

A special parliamentary sitting has been announced on November 30, 2026, bringing renewed focus to the delimitation debate after more than 100 days without prorogation following the August 13 monsoon adjournment.

The Union government is set to bring an amended Delimitation Bill that proposes a uniform 50% increase in Lok Sabha seats, extends the 1971 Census freeze on state seat shares for 25 years and uses the 2011 Census to redraw constituencies within each state.

The legislation failed to secure the required two-thirds majority in the Lok Sabha when it was put to a vote in April 2026, with the opposition citing concerns about the government’s move to link women’s reservation with delimitation based on the 2011 Census. They also pointed out the absence of a clear guarantee that the representation of all States in the Lok Sabha would increase uniformly by 50%, as the government had claimed.
Why the numbers matter in the renewed push for delimitation | Explained
Delimitation: how to align what is said and what is written

Delimitation is the process of fixing the number of seats and boundaries of the territorial constituencies in each State for the Lok Sabha and Legislative Assemblies. This ‘Delimitation process’ is performed by a higher-power body called the ‘Delimitation Commission’ that is set up under an act of Parliament. Such exercises have previously been conducted based on the 1951, 1961, and 1971 Censuses. The last time the number of seats was determined was on the basis of 1971 census population.

The current Delimitation Bill aims to significantly expand the Lok Sabha from 543 to 850 seats (815 from States, 35 from Union Territories), acknowledging the substantial population growth in India based on the latest census figures. This bill will officially end the 50-year “freeze” on reallocating seats between States, allowing for a redistribution based on current population trends. Opposition have voiced concern that the exercise could have significant consequences for political power and influence at both the State and National levels.

In April, the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill failed to win two-thirds of the majority to amend the Constitution. Out of 528 members present and voting in the Lok Sabha, 298 voted in favour and 230 voted against, falling short of the 352 votes needed.
Because the constitutional amendment did not pass, the government shelved the companion Delimitation Bill and Union Territories Laws (Amendment) Bill, stating they could not be viewed in isolation

A major concern back in April was how seats would be allocated across states. The tabled text linked delimitation to the latest published census, which was the 2011 census, rather than writing a guaranteed proportional seat share into the bill. Following through with it would have reduced the share of southern, eastern, and northeastern states due to their lower population growth relative to the Hindi heartland states.
Home Minister Amit Shah offered a verbal assurance of a 50% pro rata increase and floated redrafting it, but the opposition rejected this since the written text pointed elsewhere.

Opposition parties also objected to tying one-third reservation for women to delimitation and rushing the package through Parliament. Under the 106th Constitutional Amendment passed in 2023, women’s reservation was linked to delimitation following the next census , whereas the 131st Amendment proposed raising the Lok Sabha ceiling from 550 to 850 and linking women’s quota implementation to delimitation based on the 2011 census.

articles.title: Punjab polls: SAD, BJP reunification puts both parties back in the reckoning
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Had they contested separately, the SAD and the BJP would likely have split the Opposition space, leaving the AAP and the Congress as the principal rivals; united, they have become serious contenders

The reunification of the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) and the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) ahead of the crucial 2027 Punjab Assembly election has put both parties back in the reckoning, even as the State’s political landscape looks headed for a four-cornered fight, with the old partners joining hands to make it more competitive.

In the run-up to the election, due in early 2027, the political positioning of the parties appeared increasingly vulnerable, and political observers felt that the logical way to overcome it was to forge an alliance.
